By WT mod (which I'm assuming stands for walkthrough) do you mean the guide mod? You're using it?

If the missed events are for Ayane I'm guessing you missed 'Prisoner' which is an event with a lust requirement (10 lust with Ayane). Some of the hints on the hint screen will have a '!' next to them, make sure you click them to see specific requirements/information about events when you notice them.

If you're using the mod and no hints appear then in my experience that usually means the next event is an automatic one and it's just not showing so just skip through a few days until something happens.

If I'm wrong and you're not using the mod at all then the best advice I can give is to download and install the guide mod lol

As far as prioritising goes the mod will tell you when that needs to be done, otherwise if there's a bunch of available character events just do them in whatever order really. The only instance you might not've already passed where it matters is that you need to hold off on going to the onsen with Chika until after you've done Yumi's event 'Abyss'.

If you're enjoying the game as the actual game it is, feel free to avoid AutoVN. It's completely optional and just fixes the need to grind which a lot of people hate. That tip to read the game files and URM is overreaching too, you don't need it. The wiki can help enough for events that you're stuck on if you're at the point of giving up. URM is mainly used to skip grind without AutoVN (Though bad use of checking missed paths can break saves)

It just sounds like you were using the guide mod badly, focusing on affection events which progress the game, while ignoring lust event grinding, which you can build up in the time between affection events which the game will wait for.

Most of the guide mod events should be fixed, I was able to push a lot of fixes (There' a Karin event that they couldn't figure out, and I think one of the fixes were sub-par but I can't remember which)

posts.content_html_raw:
URM became a must-have when sensei-quest was introduced.

(yes, you can do it without it. But before that, with the exception of extra Himawari scenes, grinding was barely a thing - at most you'd have to fast-forward through 5 repeatable scenes, and that takes like two minutes).
*I do agree with shmurfer that beginners who don't take the time to understand URM can easily mess up their save though (not that it's difficult to understand). But, in comparison to the guide mod, which is stupid-proof - it can lead to problems, yes.

Good rule of thumb is: if you're on your first playthrough, don't modify anything with URM with the exception of two cases. They are:

1. if you somehow missed an event because you didn't have enough affection/lust and can't roll back, 2. sensei-quest.

Other than that, just play the game normally, and when URM notifies you about different paths, see them if you want, THEN ROLL BACK and take your actual indicated choice.

Yesterday(today?) at 3 am I was crashing out writing a post about Sensei, but I'm glad I didn't post it since it was unnecessarily emotionally charged. Now with a clearer mind, I do still feel the need to write something.

The thing about Sensei is that
Akira needs to get his shit together. We simply cannot just keep having a protagonist that remains useless for the rest of the story. Like yeah the girls are growing and all, they are carrying the storyline forward, but Akira is the protagonist whose story we are following, he has to change in some way otherwise what's the point, might as well just choose another protagonist to follow like Ayane or Ami

I'm not like Niki who deluded herself into thinking he could become a better, good person. Whether he chooses to become good or evil, it doesn't matter as long as he finally starts growing. Anything but stagnation.

The issue is, he is in a state of stasis. It has nothing to do with Maya's reset, not wanting to hurt anyone, the sealing of his memories, the timeloops, Sekai's death...

Those are just excuses for not wanting to grow up. The real issue is that he still hasn't opened the door. He is still stuck in the closet. He never left. All he ever did was get swept by the wishes & desires of Sekai. It was passing storm.

What was his hobby? poetry, because Sekai was a poet. What was the dream job he put on all of the high school surveys? Teacher, because Sekai was one.

He has never being his own person. Perhaps if this was the beginning of chapter 4, I would have pitied and felt sad for him, but now it is simply getting tiring.

The only time he ever stood up for himself during that time period was in [Kyoto]. And sadly that didn't end well (whether the [Kyoto] path could have been the better choice is up for debate). But he cannot let that past choice from holding him in place.

Nobody can save him. Even if they could, he would refuse their help. There is no choice or path for him to walk, because he has never even taken the first step by himself. "The only one who can save you is yourself". Not the girls, not the Gods, nor the readers/watchers.

You know I understand Pareidolia, and why he was important for Akira, and for us readers.
He was an excuse. Something for Akira to fight against. A fake obstacle for him to overcome. What has Akira done ever since Pareidolia left? nothing. I wish Akira struggled. At least even if he kept being pushed down while trying his best to resist, I would have the heart to cheer him on. But instead he does absolutely nothing.

I know what he wants. He wants to go back to being chapter 1 Sensei. The one with the giant cock, teacher position with the power to abuse his students. The one who can easily swoon girls left and right, the emotionless sex machine that cares for no one but his own pleasure

But that was never him. That was just a patchwork shell made up of the two people who both destroyed and influenced his life the most. Nozomu and Sekai.

The real him is just a pathetic loser who never amounted to anything. Take away his giant penis and this special circumstance of being one of the few males in Kumon-Mi, and then there is nothing he has to offer.

He has no hobbies. He has no skills. He has no wisdom.
And that's fine. He doesn't need to be special. He has a body, he has a brain, and "infinite" time. He just needs to keep fucking trying instead of just standing there being whiny little bitch.

If all he can offer is his penis and semen, then he might as well lobotomize himself and become a warm fleshy dildo for them. Same difference as to how he has been acting.

Like what is he waiting for? For someone else to get reset so that he has another excuse to shut himself out for another 2 months? then rinse and repeat?

Yesterday(today?) at 3 am I was crashing out writing a post about Sensei, but I'm glad I didn't post it since it was unnecessarily emotionally charged. Now with a clearer mind, I do still feel the need to write something.

The thing about Sensei is that
Akira needs to get his shit together. We simply cannot just keep having a protagonist that remains useless for the rest of the story. Like yeah the girls are growing and all, they are carrying the storyline forward, but Akira is the protagonist whose story we are following, he has to change in some way otherwise what's the point, might as well just choose another protagonist to follow like Ayane or Ami

I'm not like Niki who deluded herself into thinking he could become a better, good person. Whether he chooses to become good or evil, it doesn't matter as long as he finally starts growing. Anything but stagnation.

The issue is, he is in a state of stasis. It has nothing to do with Maya's reset, not wanting to hurt anyone, the sealing of his memories, the timeloops, Sekai's death...

Those are just excuses for not wanting to grow up. The real issue is that he still hasn't opened the door. He is still stuck in the closet. He never left. All he ever did was get swept by the wishes & desires of Sekai. It was passing storm.

What was his hobby? poetry, because Sekai was a poet. What was the dream job he put on all of the high school surveys? Teacher, because Sekai was one.

He has never being his own person. Perhaps if this was the beginning of chapter 4, I would have pitied and felt sad for him, but now it is simply getting tiring.

The only time he ever stood up for himself during that time period was in [Kyoto]. And sadly that didn't end well (whether the [Kyoto] path could have been the better choice is up for debate). But he cannot let that past choice from holding him in place.

Nobody can save him. Even if they could, he would refuse their help. There is no choice or path for him to walk, because he has never even taken the first step by himself. "The only one who can save you is yourself". Not the girls, not the Gods, nor the readers/watchers.

You know I understand Pareidolia, and why he was important for Akira, and for us readers.
He was an excuse. Something for Akira to fight against. A fake obstacle for him to overcome. What has Akira done ever since Pareidolia left? nothing. I wish Akira struggled. At least even if he kept being pushed down while trying his best to resist, I would have the heart to cheer him on. But instead he does absolutely nothing.

I know what he wants. He wants to go back to being chapter 1 Sensei. The one with the giant cock, teacher position with the power to abuse his students. The one who can easily swoon girls left and right, the emotionless sex machine that cares for no one but his own pleasure

But that was never him. That was just a patchwork shell made up of the two people who both destroyed and influenced his life the most. Nozomu and Sekai.

The real him is just a pathetic loser who never amounted to anything. Take away his giant penis and this special circumstance of being one of the few males in Kumon-Mi, and then there is nothing he has to offer.

He has no hobbies. He has no skills. He has no wisdom.
And that's fine. He doesn't need to be special. He has a body, he has a brain, and "infinite" time. He just needs to keep fucking trying instead of just standing there being whiny little bitch.

If all he can offer is his penis and semen, then he might as well lobotomize himself and become a warm fleshy dildo for them. Same difference as to how he has been acting.

Like what is he waiting for? For someone else to get reset so that he has another excuse to shut himself out for another 2 months? then rinse and repeat?

Otoha was one of the most hated character for a while. Not because she was an eldricht seriel stabber, but she was so realistic in the sense that you have probably saw similar people in the high school or college.

She lies about homophobic parents so her relationship with Rin never gets too serious.
She cheats on her.
She sexually assault Niki.

She knows all of them are bad, she accepts being a bad person. But she buys a gift for Niki, to apologize, to amend things.
She doesn't want to stay like this.

Kirin, i don't give a shit about her so i will keep it short. She is a slutty whore who doesn't want to be a slutty whore anymore.


Yuki beat people, used drugs, beat people to use drugs, abondoned her daughter to use drugs.

She knows she is a bad person and she thinks she doesn't deserve good things because of past regrets and probability of a relapse.

Just before the lowest point of her life she talked with Akira on the phone. So Akira knows how Yuki feels about her life and whatnot. In the preview of 0.51 Akira sees Yuki AFTER her lowest point of her life. Maybe this with combination of other events would cause something to stir up inside him. Something other than his dick for once.
And there is a third problem. We know what Sensei sees. But we have very little idea of what Sensei remembers. This causes Sensei to look like a passive, coward, lazy, retarted, detached, uncurious. Mike.Ross80 said:
Have there been other characters that talked to Akira about what Sakai did though?
Click to expand...
A lot of characters have in different levels.
Akira did confront her directly a few times, both the ghost Sekai and Alt Sekai during the last reset. However, in Akira's case, any "confrontation" is a term used very loosely and without consequence.

Pareidolia and HOPE both did to an extent, but you can imagine that it wouldn't be putting Sekai in a bad light. I don't recall if Wires did, but it's likely.

Io outright condemned Sekai and pointed out how Akira is just lying to himself in "Stomachache".

Maki also did in her event, but that spiralled into Akira defending Sekai (for the reasons we now know).

Osako condemned her multiple times now, but that didn't really go anywhere.

Wakana also condemned her tacitly, because she didn't want to force the issue even further, but logic would dictate that she knows. However, who knows with Selebus recent very questionable policy of who knows what, when it's convenient but unlikely.

Both New Maya and Maya Prime confronted him about her to different levels. But those condemnations were light given that they derived from a comparison between her situation with him, and his with Sekai - and, well, Maya loves him and doesn't want out of it in the first place - so that goes nowhere.

Niki was just the most straight to the point, but that only happened because narratively we (the reader) now know enough about the situation through Noriko's conversation, that Selebus can go there.

Chances are that any character that touches on the Sekai issue from this point on will be able to go much further than before because it isn't a mystery anymore to us. Cat's out of the bag.
I do agree that I hope Wakana's focus is on Ami though. My wish for Akira is for him to be put under medical care or straight up castrated - and I don't see Wakana doing that for him.

posts.content_html_raw:
I finally found time to write up some detailed thoughts on 0.50, which I felt the need to do because I hated this update. Hated, hated, hated it. If this update had one theme, it was throwing away character development and cohesive story in favor of filling up the quota of "girls who are aware of Sensei's harem and yet somehow still want to fuck him". In my opinion, the Sara and Nakayarakawayama events were so garbage that at least three of them (Sara's "Two For the Price of One" and "The Puppeteer", Niki's "Beauty in What's Broken") are in contention for worst in the entire game.

Warning: The following was written mostly as a way to vent. It's long, rambling, and full of snark.
Selebus keeps writing an annoyingly predictable series of events that I'm going to refer to as "the sadness pipeline" for lack of a better name.
  1. Girl finds out that Sensei has done something reprehensible.
  2. Girl gets sad and avoids Sensei for a while.
  3. ????
  4. Girl suddenly gets over her sadness and goes back to Sensei.
  5. After a single reconciliation scene (if we're lucky), their relationship goes back to normal and it's like the whole thing never happened.
By my count Molly, Noriko, Io, Chika, and now Sara have gone through the sadness pipeline, with Niki soon to join them. I really thought things would go differently with Sara because, you know, she's a responsible(ish) adult. But apparently that was completely irrelevant.

Reasons that the sadness pipeline is bad writing:
  • It's repetitive and makes the stories of very different characters feel the same.
  • Step 3 should be the most important part (and most interesting!), but Selebus has mostly left it off-screen and what we do see is woefully inadequate to justify step 4.
  • It establishes a pattern that Sensei will never face consequences for his actions, which kills any tension in the game. Will Character X manage to discover Sensei's depravity? Who cares, their relationship will end up in the same place either way.
I get that a central theme of Chapter 4 is that the world won't allow Sensei to face consequences, but if you force your characters to act in unnatural ways, it begins to feel like they lack free will. And characters without free will aren't really characters at all, they're just plot devices.
TLDR: Selebus apparently predetermined that he needed to get Sara in the harem as fast as possible and came up with a contrived way to justify it, rather than stopping to consider how his characters would organically react to events as they experienced them. In the process, he removed all nuance from her character and made her completely defined by a single thought ("I will do anything to make my daughter happy"), just like Chapter 4 Sana is defined by her own single thought ("I will do anything to get Sensei's cock").

- Apparently it only took a week or two for Sara to get over an incredibly traumatic experience and the knowledge that her daughter and her boyfriend lied to her and betrayed her trust. Her block is now gone, so I guess she's gone right back to fucking Sensei while pretending nothing happened.

- The transition from "Two for the Price of One" to "The Puppeteer" gave me whiplash. The former ends with Sara at absolute rock bottom after a very shameful orgasm, wishing she could be "put out of her misery". When the latter starts, Sara is outwardly cheerful again, and the narrator says she's only "somewhat conflicted" about the Sana situation. What the fuck happened in between? Yet again the most pivotal moment of the sadness pipeline happened off-screen.

(There's some indication that god(s) are influencing her thoughts and in particular making her unnaturally horny like they did to Sana in Chapter 3. That can explain why she impulsively masturbated listening to Sana, but it doesn't explain why she made such a life-altering change after the horniness wore off and the shame replaced it.)

- We're supposedly given Sara's justification for her decision when we're shown her thoughts, where she struggles with an internal conflict of "I'm a worthless mother if I can't make my daughter happy" vs. a vague feeling that sharing Sensei would be immoral - of course the former wins out. It's consistent with her character for her to worry about this; it's well-established that she has an inferiority complex and values her children above all else. The big problem, and why I hated these events, is that this was essentially the only thought she was allowed to have. Someone who is spiraling magnifies every minor problem to be the end of the world, they don't ignore them all to hyperfixate on one issue.

Where's the consideration of her own feelings? Does she still love Sensei? Is it even possible for her to love him with what she now knows? Has she rethought their relationship at all? Is staying with him what will make her happiest in the future, now that it's clear he's just leading her on? What about what she learned about his actions - does she feel any sense of responsibility for the other girls or for informing the other parents? Does she even care that Haruka is also a predator and has been sleeping with her boyfriend behind her back?

Even if her thoughts concentrate on the thing most important to her (Sana), all these other issues should be eating at her as well. And even her thoughts about Sana lack any nuance. Is making Sana happy more important than doing what's best for her? How about her happiness now vs her happiness later - is this "relationship" just a teenage infatuation? Would she herself have been happy staying with her own teacher, even knowing that he was using her and sleeping around? What about the very real possibility that Sensei abandons Sana the same way that Sara's teacher abandoned her? She thinks that Sana will be broken the same way she was, so why doesn't that weigh against short-term happiness?

A couple of these questions are very briefly touched on in her conversation with Ayane - she says that she now realizes that Sensei was using her, but also that she's terrified of being alone again. Wow, what a great setup for internal conflict! It sure would be a shame if she literally never thinks about these things again!

- Ayane also asks why she isn't more upset about the immorality of Sensei's actions, and she gives this response:
First, this is a complete non-answer: she can't judge the girls for doing the same things she did, but that's irrelevant to whether she can judge Sensei for doing the same things her teacher did. Where's the righteous anger she feels whenever he comes up? Maybe she's deflecting the question, but Ayane doesn't act like it.

Second, this equating her relationship with her children makes no sense. She doesn't regret having her children, but she certainly regrets trusting her teacher and blames him for ruining her family's lives. Is she expecting Sensei to knock up all of the girls so they can be as miserable happy as she was?

Third, she essentially contradicted this idea earlier in the very same event:
She's terrified of Sana following in her footsteps when those footsteps represent the best choice she ever made?

- What the fuck was the point of Nodokathon (or for that matter, Ayane's confession) if Sara is going to completely ignore all of it except for "my daughter is fucking my boyfriend and wants us to share him"? She could have just caught Sana in the act with Sensei (either planned by Sana or not) and Sana could suggest a threesome later. If it's essential that Sensei doesn't know, just have Sana be the only one to notice Sara entering the room or something. That would get the plot to the same place without all the contrived decision-making that was necessary for the Nodokathon event to happen, with the added bonus that Sara wouldn't need to conspicuously avoid thinking about all of the other things she learned.

- Sara is supposedly unable to say no to Sana, but obviously there are exceptions given she kept seeing Sensei even though Sana was firmly against it and asked her not to.

- Sara and Sana both say the two of them aren't very close, which is a little bizarre. We've seen a bunch of events of them bonding, and they're clearly closer than any other parent and child we're actually shown in the game. (No, Moonflare, I'm not counting Himawari ) There have been some mentions that Sana doesn't always want to hang out with Sara, but that's just normal teenager stuff.

- Ayane is the latest character to reduce what's going on with Sana to "I guess she's just a pervert and we have to learn to live with it." Embracing her perversion doesn't explain why the rest of Sana's personality just... disappeared. Perversion is not some magical cure for crippling shyness. You can be a complete degenerate with your sexual partners without letting it destroy all of your other relationships.

- The music selection in these scenes sucks. The generic bar music works for melancholy, not abject despair. The music from critically acclaimed event Ad Infinitum works great for uncanny scenes where a character sees hints of the supernatural underpinnings of the world, not so much for traumatic memories of parental abuse. The generic upbeat music in "The Puppeteer" just emphasizes the complete lack of emotional weight.
I eagerly await the scene commentary for "Beauty in What's Broken", where I fully expect Selebus to reveal to us:
"Niki kind of forgot about what she and Ami said to each other at Christmas."

The last time Niki and Ami talked ("Seed of Self-Doubt"), it had an explosive ending on the Bad Uncle path in which Ami revealed she was manipulating Niki to try to get her to leave, Ami told Niki that her dad was "hypothetically" already fucking her as well as all of her friends, and Niki tried to get Ami to talk about it. This was obviously a big cliffhanger setting up for the next time they interacted, and yet none of it was acknowledged at any point in this update. Their conversation is literally identical whether the Christmas confrontation happened or not (the Bad Uncle flag is never checked).

Honestly, it's pretty comical when you compare the two side by side:
Niki at Christmas:

Niki now after at least a month of apparently still not having that talk with Ami:
Niki then:

Niki now:
Niki then:

Niki now:
Ami then:

Ami now:

I guess the most charitable interpretation is that the gods forced Niki to forget about Christmas, even though there's no hint that anything like that happened to her. Of course they also would have needed to manipulate her thoughts to make her completely change her mind about how to deal with Ami, make her unwilling to entertain the possibility that Ami's talk is more than fantasy, etc.

The far more likely explanation is that Selebus decided Niki walking in on Noriko would be more impactful if she was completely blindsided by the idea that Sensei might fuck teenagers. So he retconned Niki to be in total denial instead of actively trying to find out the truth. Of course the Christmas scene still remains in the game, completely vestigial to the story that was actually told. It's a shame because that scene was far stronger than what replaced it, and also far more interesting since it made Niki unique as a character instead of just one more member of the willful ignorance club.
For those keeping track at home, here is what Ami the master schemer has done to get rid of Niki:
  1. Let Niki move in with Sensei - he said it wouldn't happen if Ami objected.
  2. Act like an incest gremlin for months, apparently to disgust Niki into leaving, but otherwise do nothing to convince Niki that her talk is more than just fantasies.
  3. Straight up reveal to Niki that Ami's been trying to manipulate her into leaving and doesn't love her.
  4. Suggest that Sensei might actually be fucking her and her friends, but still don't unambiguously say that he is.
  5. Wait at least another month while continuing to do nothing, until Niki suggests a weekend away without Sensei.
  6. Only now arrange for Niki to discover Sensei fucking someone else.
If this was her plan all along, why didn't she do it ages ago? None of the pivotal scenes even happened at their house, so what was the point of letting Niki move in? This is all so erratic that it makes it seem like someone is making things up as they go along: either Ami or Selebus. I'm really worried it's the latter given Niki's own 180 in her interactions with Ami.

In the process, he removed all nuance from her character and made her completely defined by a single thought ("I will do anything to make my daughter happy"), just like Chapter 4 Sana is defined by her own single thought ("I will do anything to get Sensei's cock").
- Apparently it only took a week or two for Sara to get over an incredibly traumatic experience and the knowledge that her daughter and her boyfriend lied to her and betrayed her trust. Her block is now gone, so I guess she's gone right back to fucking Sensei while pretending nothing happened.
- The transition from "Two for the Price of One" to "The Puppeteer" gave me whiplash. The former ends with Sara at absolute rock bottom after a very shameful orgasm, wishing she could be "put out of her misery". When the latter starts, Sara is outwardly cheerful again, and the narrator says she's only "somewhat conflicted" about the Sana situation. What the fuck happened in between? Yet again the most pivotal moment of the sadness pipeline happened off-screen.
(There's some indication that god(s) are influencing her thoughts and in particular making her unnaturally horny like they did to Sana in Chapter 3. That can explain why she impulsively masturbated listening to Sana, but it doesn't explain why she made such a life-altering change after the horniness wore off and the shame replaced it.)
- We're supposedly given Sara's justification for her decision when we're shown her thoughts, where she struggles with an internal conflict of "I'm a worthless mother if I can't make my daughter happy" vs. a vague feeling that sharing Sensei would be immoral - of course the former wins out. It's consistent with her character for her to worry about this; it's well-established that she has an inferiority complex and values her children above all else. only

possible

Spoiler

miserable
happy as she was?

Spoiler

spoilers.title: Niki & Ami
spoilers.html:
I eagerly await the scene commentary for "Beauty in What's Broken", where I fully expect Selebus to reveal to us:
"Niki kind of forgot about what she and Ami said to each other at Christmas."

The last time Niki and Ami talked ("Seed of Self-Doubt"), it had an explosive ending on the Bad Uncle path in which Ami revealed she was manipulating Niki to try to get her to leave, Ami told Niki that her dad was "hypothetically" already fucking her as well as all of her friends, and Niki tried to get Ami to talk about it. This was obviously a big cliffhanger setting up for the next time they interacted, and yet none of it was acknowledged at any point in this update. Their conversation is literally identical whether the Christmas confrontation happened or not (the Bad Uncle flag is never checked).

Honestly, it's pretty comical when you compare the two side by side:

I guess the most charitable interpretation is that the gods forced Niki to forget about Christmas, even though there's no hint that anything like that happened to her. Of course they also would have needed to manipulate her thoughts to make her completely change her mind about how to deal with Ami, make her unwilling to entertain the possibility that Ami's talk is more than fantasy, etc.

The far more likely explanation is that Selebus decided Niki walking in on Noriko would be more impactful if she was completely blindsided by the idea that Sensei might fuck teenagers. So he retconned Niki to be in total denial instead of actively trying to find out the truth. Of course the Christmas scene still remains in the game, completely vestigial to the story that was actually told. It's a shame because that scene was far stronger than what replaced it, and also far more interesting since it made Niki unique as a character instead of just one more member of the willful ignorance club.

spoilers.title: Ami's master plan
spoilers.html:
For those keeping track at home, here is what Ami the master schemer has done to get rid of Niki:
  1. Let Niki move in with Sensei - he said it wouldn't happen if Ami objected.
  2. Act like an incest gremlin for months, apparently to disgust Niki into leaving, but otherwise do nothing to convince Niki that her talk is more than just fantasies.
  3. Straight up reveal to Niki that Ami's been trying to manipulate her into leaving and doesn't love her.
  4. Suggest that Sensei might actually be fucking her and her friends, but still don't unambiguously say that he is.
  5. Wait at least another month while continuing to do nothing, until Niki suggests a weekend away without Sensei.
  6. Only now arrange for Niki to discover Sensei fucking someone else.
If this was her plan all along, why didn't she do it ages ago? None of the pivotal scenes even happened at their house, so what was the point of letting Niki move in? This is all so erratic that it makes it seem like someone is making things up as they go along: either Ami or Selebus. I'm really worried it's the latter given Niki's own 180 in her interactions with Ami.

The Maya thing is getting kind of silly as well. She supposedly raped New Maya to turn her into a "pet" and control her with threats. But so far all she's used that control for is to prevent Maya from telling Sensei about her (which doesn't seem like it's going to last much longer) and has accomplished nothing other than making Maya hate her. What's the point?

Meanwhile, she also seems to be pushing New Maya and Sensei together. Shortly after her breakdown, she sent Maya to meet Sensei at the shrine, fully expecting them to have sex. Now she organized this box thing to break down some of the barriers between them. But then she shows up at the dorm to cockblock them and prevent their night from ending in sex. Why is she helping them to get closer if she doesn't want them to fuck, especially after being the one to orchestrate it earlier?

spoilers.title: Noriko & Sensei
spoilers.html:
Hey guys I wrote a new Noriko event, I hope you like it:
Noriko: I love you, Onii-chan.
Sensei: I am a pathetic person and not worthy of your love.
Noriko: I care not, for my love is unlimited and unconditional.
Sensei: I basically kidnapped an eight-year-old off the street so that I could groom her into the perfect loli girlfriend. I fucked my codependent daughter's throat right in front of you.
Noriko: Everyone makes mistakes. I would like to fornicate with you now.
Sensei: I too would like to fornicate with you.
...
Noriko: Wait, this is all happening too fast.
Sensei: I would still like to fornicate with you but I no longer believe this is the appropriate time to do so. This does not deter me and I will proceed to fornicate with you anyway.

The End.
I hereby grant Selebus permission to use this text. It could save a lot of unnecessary words, maybe then he would have the space to give Sara and Niki character arcs which are actually believable.

- While reading these scenes, an analogy come to mind: Noriko is like an actress attempting to play the lead in a heartfelt romantic drama despite having zero chemistry with her co-star. She's reading the lines, but the feeling behind them is artificial. I think it's because her feelings are so straightforward and unchanging that they feel unearned. There's no room for "deepening their bond" when Noriko literally can't love Sensei more than she already does at the beginning of the game. They can't really talk about anything else because Noriko turns every topic back into how much she loves Sensei (the one sort-of exception is her "rivalry" with Maya, which ultimately comes back to Sensei anyway). There's no drama because she's unwilling to critically examine her feelings or actually judge Sensei for any of his "mistakes".

- Having Sensei finally make the Nozomu reveal to Noriko of all people is such a lame choice. She's probably the only person in the entire game who won't let it affect the way she feels about Sensei in any way, and she has a history of keeping all of Sensei's secrets. I fully expect this to be yet another plot point that is ignored for months.

- The poems that give "Haiku" its title aren't even real haiku. Where are the kigo, Selebus, you fucking hack? Just kidding. Mostly.

- Did Noriko really bring up Maya just so that... she can make a joke about how Sensei repeatedly raped a child? Seriously?
Glad we're all on the same page that this is what she should have been worried about, not the grooming victim's mental well-being and stunted development.

spoilers.title: Noriko & Niki
spoilers.html:
- The sex scene starts with an extended attempt at purely erotic writing, something I can't remember Selebus doing for a while, and it's really out of place here. For one, Sensei is once again using sex to escape thinking about his trauma (Nozomu this time), and when that happens he usually gets really creepy with it (e.g. "Stomachache", "Now & Forever") or at the very least pathetically self-reflective (e.g. "How to Make Love Stay"). So when he thinks about only the mechanics of what's happening, it's a departure. More importantly, though, it's hard to read this as a sex scene at all; instead, I'm impatiently waiting for Niki to walk in on them, since that's been telegraphed since the start of the event chain.

- There's some good dialogue in these scenes ("You were there when she was born. She quite literally can not have known you just as long." is a banger), but when I'm reading it I'm not feeling any of the intended emotions, instead just boredom and exasperation. To get here, one of the most interesting events in Chapter 4 had to be retconned. And for what? To have one more girl in willful ignorance so that one more girl can enter the sadness pipeline. Earlier in this very update, Sara reminded us that the sadness pipeline will probably end illogically and abruptly with no meaningful effect, so it's hard to believe that Niki "finding out" will really matter. This is especially true when she's already broadcasting that she's halfway to step 4; she isn't breaking up with Sensei and she isn't moving out.

- I guess the conversation between Sensei and Niki is alright, but it barely even feels like a dialogue due to Sensei's current state of being sad, pathetic, and unwilling to change. Instead it's just the two of them making explicit some feelings that were already pretty clear from their actions, and Niki (justifiably) berating him for being a sack of shit. I'm just so sick of reading about Chapter 4 Sensei at this point, it's repetitive and getting in the way of the development of actually interesting characters.

daagagsdgd said:
What do you guys think of Akira (or Nozomu) being secret son of Miu? I'm at odds with it but I can't quite come up a feasible counterargument. The hair colour of Akira has a shade of red coming from nowhere unless from Yuu that is. But the doddle of Upside Down House has no implication of another red hair character other than Miu. Also, with Akira being bastard son of Yuu, the weird hostility from Saki and Nozomu targeting him as the one made Yuu crazy tracks.

Also Ami has pure red hair, just like Sekai while we don't know the hair color of Nozomu. If he's also black with a tint of red, shouldn't Ami has lighter hair color? The same logic goes with Akira being her potential father.
Click to expand...
A low-hanging counterargument would come from just how young Miu looks like in A House Near a Lake. Nozomu is presumed to be close in age with Sekai, meaning Miu would have to be pregnant with Akira at a time considerably later than Saki being pregnant with Nozomu. And here a pregnant Miu shown in A House Near a Lake looks and acts still like just a highschooler; it'd be pretty wild to think that at the moment of A House Near a Lake, Saki's already given birth to Nozomu and Nozomu has already been kicking for some years.

Three counter-counters to stab this counterargument though:
- Maybe Nozomu and Akira are actually not too far apart in ages, and Sekai (in this assumption she is someone not blood-related to Arakawa) might also be significantly older than Nozomu instead of being in the same age group with her husband. Not very solid theory though as I think there might already be pre-established knowledge somewhere that can overthrow this but as of now I couldn't remember any detail.

- The way how Miu looks in A House Near a Lake isn't something that bears much additional meaning, just like how every time Saki in past events showed up only in her highschooler form, even when Yasu reminded Sensei of her name and subsequently her imagery (though pixelated). Her limited sprite is used only for "this person is Miu" and nothing more.

- Miu simply got pregnant with Akira at a much later time, her second pregnancy. What is shown in A House Near a Lake is her first time, carrying just Sekai. This doesn’t have an apparent hole yet, other than explaining the necessity of assuming Akira potentially being Miu’s son in the first place.

posts.content_html_raw:
So to finally write something that has nothing to do with how much I've come to hate Akira and chapter 4,
For a while I have been wanting to theorize and predict what's going on in Kumon-Mi, and what's going to happen in the future. Or well, lack of future for this world.

But the problem is, I don't even know what the fuck Kumon-Mi is.

Is it a different dimension with different rules? Is it a simulation? Is it a dream? Is it a world within a world within a world? Is it a God's garden/domain? A combination of different things?

I don't think the answer is simulation. Selebus really loves making fun of the simulation-theorists, inside and outside the game. So after talking all that smack it would be crazy for him to just go "YOU ABSOLUTE BUFFOON! NEANDERTHALE! It was reverse psychology all along! I had fun leading you imbecile astray! OCCAM'S RAZOR YOU FOOL"

But the problem is that Selebus simply LOVES to borrow from simulation/computer-like vocabulary. USERS, Terminals, Wires, ERRORS, Hexadecimals, Attempts to connect, resets, auto-pilot, etc.

If not simulation, why simulation shape?
One way to justify all of that computer mumbo jumbo is that using those words is how it can be explained to the human brain.
Meaning, whatever is talking to us, narrator, Gods, or something, is translating its words into computer terminology because we cannot comprehend its original intent, because we cannot fathom the minds and means of Gods or magical shit, and so words like "terminal" and "USER" is the closest comparison.

But anyways, the problem with my theory about the future of this world is that I have inevitably written it using simulation-like terminology, despite the fact I do not subscribe to the simulation theory.

Like the more I try to speculate about this world, the more my own theory leads into the simulation route

So to finally write something that has nothing to do with how much I've come to hate Akira and chapter 4,
For a while I have been wanting to theorize and predict what's going on in Kumon-Mi, and what's going to happen in the future. Or well, lack of future for this world.

Is it a different dimension with different rules? Is it a simulation? Is it a dream? Is it a world within a world within a world? Is it a God's garden/domain? A combination of different things?

I don't think the answer is simulation. Selebus really loves making fun of the simulation-theorists, inside and outside the game. So after talking all that smack it would be crazy for him to just go "YOU ABSOLUTE BUFFOON! NEANDERTHALE! It was reverse psychology all along! I had fun leading you imbecile astray! OCCAM'S RAZOR YOU FOOL"

But the problem is that Selebus simply LOVES to borrow from simulation/computer-like vocabulary. USERS, Terminals, Wires, ERRORS, Hexadecimals, Attempts to connect, resets, auto-pilot, etc.

If not simulation, why simulation shape?
One way to justify all of that computer mumbo jumbo is that using those words is how it can be explained to the human brain.
Meaning, whatever is talking to us, narrator, Gods, or something, is translating its words into computer terminology because we cannot comprehend its original intent, because we cannot fathom the minds and means of Gods or magical shit, and so words like "terminal" and "USER" is the closest comparison.

People are arguing two different things when it comes to simulation discussions. The thing they don't want is for the events of the game to have not mattered because Akira woke up and then continued with his life, like it was all a dream for one night.

But there's no problem if the simulation is essentially the matrix. Akira is the one, there is some objective that needs to happen regarding him, and there might be a mixture of real and artificial characters / girls in the simulation with him. The whole thing is a sandbox, complete with love and lust values that the admins / gods can alter. They can load maps, and move actors within the maps. Maybe there's different sandboxes / terminals running at the same time.

If it is a simulation in that sense, we don't know what the actual goal is. So far we're focused on trying to get Akira to heal from his trauma regarding Sekai and how it affects his relationships with women and sex. posts.content_html_raw:
[I think i made a similar post a long time ago.]
The whole nature of the world has been fucking over my investment in a lot of characters progressing/developments for a long time tbh. For a lot of the characters its hard to do anything consequential because of it. It does not necessarily have to be a problem. But given the amount of characters and people being invested in various combinations of characters and plot lines to different levels. It inevitably leaves some characters in a position where its basically impossible to do anything significantly meaningful with them for now. Mainly because of the world and gods stuff being progressed to the point that any buildup to anything consequential, or even the consequential moments themselves, for a lot of characters, can just end up falling flat because of said world and gods stuff being progressed to what it is now. Or more so the readers knowledge of it. ( Tangentially: I guess that same effect is probably intended to be one of the reasons Akira is so annoying in chapter 4 to some extent. If nothing matters to him he cant really not be insufferable. )

Now with that said, for myself i don't mind that to much. As the characters I'm most interested in are not the ones most fucked over by this. And I'm also probably more interested in this game from the meta perspective than most people are (at least based on things i read people getting annoyed by that i don't mind that much tbh). However, i can definitely see the game only getting more annoying and less interesting over time now If your primarily interested in characters themselves inside the kumonmi world, how they fit together, interact with each other and their development/progression in that sense and dislike a lot of the other stuff. I think its just going to get more and more Selebussy (I assume everyone will know what i mean by that) as time goes on. Probably to the detriment of the narratives/plot lines internal to kumonmi that have yet to culminate/reach any meaningful positions. And i think its inevitable that some characters will end up left by the wayside and underwhelming. I can only hope its not the ones I'm most interested in.

It's literally impossible for SubscribeStar to track what other sites you visit unless those sites import third-party resources from SubscribeStar (something like a sign-in widget). Cookies are domain-specific, so there is no way for SubscribeStar to check if you have cookies set for F95, Kemono, or whatever. Your browser will never make these cookies available to them.

I don't know how SubscribeStar integration works on the LiL site since I haven't done it myself, but I assume they do know if you've linked your account there. But I'm not sure why they would care, there's no link between that site and piracy/scraping.

What they can do (and it's well within their rights to do so) is flag your account for suspicious activity that they identify as web scraping. So it's almost certainly a bad idea to give Kemono access to your SubscribeStar session ID and let them scrape using your account. But what SubscribeStar is monitoring in this case is requests sent to their own server, not your activity on some other site.

(I'm sure some unfortunate people get falsely flagged without actually scraping anything, but it's safe to assume SubscribeStar wants to avoid this as a common occurrence since it costs them money.)

It's literally impossible for SubscribeStar to track what other sites you visit unless those sites import third-party resources from SubscribeStar (something like a sign-in widget). Cookies are domain-specific, so there is no way for SubscribeStar to check if you have cookies set for F95, Kemono, or whatever. Your browser will never make these cookies available to them.
I don't know how SubscribeStar integration works on the LiL site since I haven't done it myself, but I assume they do know if you've linked your account there. But I'm not sure why they would care, there's no link between that site and piracy/scraping.
What they can do (and it's well within their rights to do so) is flag your account for suspicious activity that they identify as web scraping. So it's almost certainly a bad idea to give Kemono access to your SubscribeStar session ID and let them scrape using your account. But what SubscribeStar is monitoring in this case is requests sent to their own server, not your activity on some other site.
(I'm sure some unfortunate people get falsely flagged without actually scraping anything, but it's safe to assume SubscribeStar wants to avoid this as a common occurrence since it costs them money.)

Given the Yuki/Tsubasa reveal and their upcoming events, I thought it would be useful to go over what we know about their respective pasts. The short version: the two of them aren't related and almost certainly first met when they were high school age (though they didn't go to school together).
Overview of Yuki's past:
  • Grew up in a small countryside town where her parents owned a candy shop. I'm guessing in Gunma, since that's where her niece Kaori is from.
  • Started high school in her hometown but dropped out to run away and join a biker gang. During this period she was extremely poor and generally homeless.
  • Sometime after ending up in Kumon-mi, but while she was still a teenager, met Yoshitsugu Yamaguchi and moved in with him. Became involved with the Yakuza and hooked on drugs.
  • Within a few years, was frequently so out of it that she could be raped without remembering (when she was 21-22). Subsequently gave birth to Yumi.
  • Years of being a bad parent, during which she was usually high.
  • When she was approximately 31-34 (based on context), abandoned Yumi, left the Yakuza, and got clean.
Candy shop in the country:

Dropped out of school to join a biker gang and escape her small town:

More on the biker gang:

Met Yumi's dad and joined the Yakuza while still a teenager:

Overview of Tsubasa's past:
  • Was born into a wealthy family where arranged marriages were standard. Her marriage to Tomonori Tsukioka was arranged from the beginning.
  • Went to the prestigious Higashigaoka Girls' Academy. Location unconfirmed, but probably near Kumon-mi since Wakana also went there.
  • Apparently went to university.
  • Married Tomonori at least 16 years ago, and has been fully focused on her family since.
Birth family - wealth, prestige, and tradition:

High school academy:

University, where she had some freedom given she was cooking for herself:

So Yuki and Tsubasa didn't just come from different social classes, but also different parts of the country - I'm assuming Tsubasa's family, with its wealth and prestige, did not live in a small countryside town. Yuki first came to Kumon-mi at most 23 years ago. Her drug addiction started at least 19 years ago, after which I doubt she was in a state to form close relationships. It seems to me she had to have met Tsubasa in between the two.

In fact, there was opportunity for them to meet in that period. When Tsubasa was in high school, she would sneak away to have "wild" times with "girlfriends".
Around the same time, Tsubasa played a lot of pinball.
I somehow doubt the dorms of Higashigaoka Girls' Academy had pinball tables, so it's likely she was playing at arcades - the type of place where delinquents like to hang out (see: Yumi in Chapter 1). I think this is probably where they met. Depending on the age gap, the relationship may have continued into Tsubasa's time in college.

Yuki learned bits of English from an old friend who wasn't exactly a member of her gang (I posted about this here). Given what we now know, it's very likely this was Tsubasa, who is fluent in English.

I will point out there's still a small chance that it wasn't Tsubasa; so far we haven't learned anything about her that would fit the "creative type" label. But even then it could be a mutual acquaintance of the two - and we know Tsubasa has an unexplained connection to Sekai.
On a related subject, an existing relationship between Yuki and Tsubasa gives new meaning to something from Chapter 3: Tsubasa reacted with surprise when she learned that Yumi is a Yamaguchi.
She probably realized at that point that Yumi is Yuki's daughter. She almost certainly knew at least something about Yuki's relationship with the Yakuza, given she very conveniently shows up at the Yamaguchi estate at the right time and calls Yuki "The Dragon".

Finally, a couple of very speculative thoughts that are only tangentially related to the rest of this post:
1. Tsubasa used to be an expert at pinball. Osako is also a very good pinball player.
This is a weird thing to include in the backgrounds of two different characters. It's still probably coincidence, especially given the age gap between them (at least 10 years), but it's possible they've met before (they haven't met in LiL yet).


2. In 0.50, Yuki once again told a suspiciously specific story about someone she knew when she was younger.
There's a lot of superfluous details about the girl here, just like with the friend who taught her English, so I wonder if she is similarly someone we know. If she is, my best guess is Kyoko Nagasawa. I don't think it has been established that she's physically disabled (just mentally absent) but it could explain why she was confined to a computer chair (not the normal place for a human vegetable).
It doesn't seem like Yuki knew this girl well, though, so I'm not sure if it will be important going forward.

So Yuki and Tsubasa didn't just come from different social classes, but also different parts of the country - I'm assuming Tsubasa's family, with its wealth and prestige, did not live in a small countryside town. Yuki first came to Kumon-mi at most 23 years ago. Her drug addiction started at least 19 years ago, after which I doubt she was in a state to form close relationships. It seems to me she had to have met Tsubasa in between the two.
In fact, there was opportunity for them to meet in that period. When Tsubasa was in high school, she would sneak away to have "wild" times with "girlfriends".
Spoiler
Around the same time, Tsubasa played a lot of pinball.
Spoiler
I somehow doubt the dorms of Higashigaoka Girls' Academy had pinball tables, so it's likely she was playing at arcades - the type of place where delinquents like to hang out (see: Yumi in Chapter 1). I think this is probably where they met. Depending on the age gap, the relationship may have continued into Tsubasa's time in college.
Yuki learned bits of English from an old friend who wasn't exactly a member of her gang (I posted about this
here
). Given what we now know, it's very likely this was Tsubasa, who is fluent in English.
Spoiler
I will point out there's still a small chance that it wasn't Tsubasa;
so far
we haven't learned anything about her that would fit the "creative type" label. But even then it could be a mutual acquaintance of the two - and we know Tsubasa has an unexplained connection to Sekai.

spoilers.title: possible connections
spoilers.html:
1. Tsubasa used to be an expert at pinball. Osako is also a very good pinball player.
This is a weird thing to include in the backgrounds of two different characters. It's still probably coincidence, especially given the age gap between them (at least 10 years), but it's possible they've met before (they haven't met in LiL yet).


2. In 0.50, Yuki once again told a suspiciously specific story about someone she knew when she was younger.
There's a lot of superfluous details about the girl here, just like with the friend who taught her English, so I wonder if she is similarly someone we know. If she is, my best guess is Kyoko Nagasawa. I don't think it has been established that she's physically disabled (just mentally absent) but it could explain why she was confined to a computer chair (not the normal place for a human vegetable).
It doesn't seem like Yuki knew this girl well, though, so I'm not sure if it will be important going forward.

- Tme fuckery remember? It just makes sense (Italian hand gestures).
- Selly wrote something later in the game that contradicted his own character sheets that he released on the side in an earlier date.

To me the last one sounds the most probable, as I welcome oversights a lot more than stretched assumptions. Literally all you need to do is pretend that Noriko is also written as 15 and everything will look A-okay. That way, "Ayane > Ami" and "Noriko ~ Ami" would work without anymore "maybe this or maybe that".

bubbleBubblebubbl3 said:
Is there a tldr of the drama surrounding this game somewhere?
Click to expand...
There are many.
- The real life drama is that the author is an ass with an overblown sense of the artistic merit of his game that feels he should dictate how people play it (present); add to this that he left F95 after a bunch of cringey steps to try to have his game banned from here, then followed by implementing DRMs on a couple of worthless dlc (past).

- The in-game drama is twofold. One is the rare ranting against even other developers for having "stolen" the game format, and against players for their "stupid" interpretations of the game. The other is a bit more complicated, and it has to do with the content itself:

1. Externally, although quite praised for his writing, in the last year or so, Selebus' writing has been called into question multiple times. As we have reached the middle of the story, more or less, some of his revelations don't quite track with what he presented. That coupled with some characters behaving in a less realistic manner without being properly given supernatural reasons for that, and his own declarations that 90% of the story is just him "winging it" and that some events "didn't even exist and it was just experimentation", has dragged faith down from what it used to be.

2. Internally, this past year has also deviated from the kind of content we came to expect, with now almost regular "extreme" sexual scenes between the love interests and people not the protagonist, and also poorly timed chain of events and their "tone". There's also the fact that the protagonist's "inaction" has now been going on for a very long time and people are tired of it.
*all of these can be further explained, but that's the gist of it.

Well, "dying" is an overstatement. Maya Prime was moved and is currently being held in a parallel dimension that we've taken to calling "the replica of heaven". We get to know this through Noriko's TSS, and Maya Prime is currently accompanied by AmIOkay, which is one of the Maya-like entities.

Akira realizes he loves Maya in a series of events, but if I had to pinpoint a single moment it was during the "I will deliver you to the fireflies" chain.

In the event itself he declares that he loves her, but I mention the chain because it's related to how he comes to this conclusion. First, he's confronted with the memories of Sekai, then of his own name, and is being assaulted by Sekai's memories while Noriko is about to lose her virginity with him. It's then that Maya sends him a message, and that's (imo) when he realises it.

He was losing himself into the memories of Sekai and because of the gods manipulations, and managed to wrestle free of all of them by confronting them directly after Maya contacts him, by declaring they have no place in his life anymore and that only she (Maya) does. He then starts the event by stating that she makes him feel normal again.

I don't think Selebus is stalling persay. The story is moving as it has to move regarding the end of the harem route. That means getting Akira to fuck everyone, for everyone to know about everyone else, and for a lot of threesomes to happen.
For all of this to occur, some other stuff also has to happen. For instance, there has to be some reasoning for some people that didn't fuck him yet to decide to do so. There also has to be a reason for people (especially the adults) to be "okay" with Akira being a pedophile. To do all of this in a realistic manner takes time and multiple character arcs advancing... for 35+ characters.

And, other than Akira having to be accounted on all of this - there's also the issue of not being able to focus just on those arcs, cause it'd be kind of ridiculous. So other arcs also have to advance at the same time.

All of this being said, I think his writing is leaving a lot to be desired. Yumi and Rin's overall arc is fine, and even Touka's, to an extent. Chika's is whatever, I can take it or leave it. Niki and Noriko was expected, but that went into a dangerous road in terms of the players just giving up on Akira. Sara and Sana's just weird (writing wise), and Yuki's...

Other than those, I was never a fan of Imani's romance and am ever less now (sorry, I can't buy that Imani doesn't realise things). Rika's felt super forced. Karin is also meh, but I can't see another way for it to go either. We can go on...
Anyway, I think we're seeing a consequence of a couple of factors. There are just way too many characters, there is a critical lack of planning, there have been some questionable story decisions, and Akira's not having enough of an "active" protagonist role.

And a last thing that certainly doesn't help is that LiL has always been about stalling, or rather not pursuing things any normal person would. Akira hardly ever does shit. "oh, I have found this hole to nothingness during my date with Io? better ignore it." - and he does that to everything since the first event of the game. Kind of upsetting, especially now.

posts.content_html_raw:
Eh, to be fair - Sel is a pretty good writer in AVN/Smut category. He's a fairly decent one even outside the scope of porn.

His biggest flaw right now - is the lack of planning. I've been writing a lot of stuff for the past 5 years, both fiction and non-fiction, and I've realized that if you don't plan your shit - it's gonna be all over the place. Characters will become inconsistent, story will branch and develop its own sub-narratives, the main plot is gonna be lost somewhere in a ditch. Everything's gonna get messy unless you stick to at least some sort of plan.

And honestly - the fact that most characters stayed mostly consistent throughout 5-6 years of writing on a whim - that is a fucking impressive feat.

So yeah, he's a narcissist and a very egotistical fella, but he's a decent writer.

I think ultimately it will be decided by how the story ends. Take GoT for example - great story, shittiest ending, nobody rewatches it, despite very very good first 80% of the show. Couple of years ago found a story that got me hooked for like 2 months of non-stop reading - but the author just doesn't know when to stop and keeps going and going and going and adding more to the harem and going and adding... And judging by the comments, he's been doing that for 8 years with no end in sight.

IMO - end of the story is an extremely important part and the writer's ability can't be judged until the story ends.

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
I don't think Selebus is stalling persay. The story is moving as it has to move regarding the end of the harem route. That means getting Akira to fuck everyone, for everyone to know about everyone else, and for a lot of threesomes to happen.
For all of this to occur, some other stuff also has to happen. For instance, there has to be some reasoning for some people that didn't fuck him yet to decide to do so. There also has to be a reason for people (especially the adults) to be "okay" with Akira being a pedophile. To do all of this in a realistic manner takes time and multiple character arcs advancing... for 35+ characters.

And, other than Akira having to be accounted on all of this - there's also the issue of not being able to focus just on those arcs, cause it'd be kind of ridiculous. So other arcs also have to advance at the same time.

All of this being said, I think his writing is leaving a lot to be desired. Yumi and Rin's overall arc is fine, and even Touka's, to an extent. Chika's is whatever, I can take it or leave it. Niki and Noriko was expected, but that went into a dangerous road in terms of the players just giving up on Akira. Sara and Sana's just weird (writing wise), and Yuki's...

Other than those, I was never a fan of Imani's romance and am ever less now (sorry, I can't buy that Imani doesn't realise things). Rika's felt super forced. Karin is also meh, but I can't see another way for it to go either. We can go on...
Anyway, I think we're seeing a consequence of a couple of factors. There are just way too many characters, there is a critical lack of planning, there have been some questionable story decisions, and Akira's not having enough of an "active" protagonist role.

And a last thing that certainly doesn't help is that LiL has always been about stalling, or rather not pursuing things any normal person would. Akira hardly ever does shit. "oh, I have found this hole to nothingness during my date with Io? better ignore it." - and he does that to everything since the first event of the game. Kind of upsetting, especially now.
Click to expand...
Adding some to the stalling part and this is about the stage set for Ch4. This is the chapter that started with one of the gods living inside him. This is the chapter after Maya Prime, our unshakable constant of the universe, died. This is the chapter where many, many things have fundamentally changed. Somehow, despite all that, we still could only steadily confirm that there IS progress mainly by measuring body counts. Because hey hey hey! Things might have gone dark quickly but we ain’t done with harem route! Look at all these unexplored females!

Call me naive and greedy, but my expectation for Ch4 wasn’t set to “finish fucking all the girls (minus wizards because please anything but wizards)”. Instead, with this chapter’s opening, I was fully expecting the development to be more about resets, Maya, and Sensei’s mental struggle in a much larger, more frequent, and more meaningful scale. As it turns out, it would seem like the stage is set instead to mainly bring rapid mental decay to girls that haven’t received the D and expedite the process, aka finishing the harem route as the main, prioritized objective and nothing else, as anything else would “move things forward too quickly and reveal too much too early” even if it feels like the right thing to do in Ch4 (personal bias though, of course).

This is the part where the feeling of stalling comes in for me. Story moves in all directions but rarely forwards. No one is allowed to advance too much in directions easily done by normal human standards like you implied; Maki, Imani, even Akira to a certain degree. Any forward progress would likely to be once in the blue moon only and have a high tendency to backpaddle (looking at things with Maya and Akira’s personal growth and especially Akira’s personal growth).

So what will happen when writers need to maintain the same amount of updates without venturing out too much? It can’t be just the same light hearted shoujo manga drama as before anymore but it also can’t be anything that spills too much tea you know? What should they do to make treading water look intriguing? They make things wordier and more complicated than they have to, much like the talking pattern of the renowned writer SA Nagahara, delivering sentences at a composition of 10% useful information and 90% gibberish. But hey there are more words than Bible now!

Webnovel if you really just have the narrative you want to tell and are unsure of bonus media that youd want to include.

thebladeofwar said:
I was wondering if there was a TLDR someone made of the general consensus of the deep lore.
Click to expand...
Chapter 4 has introduced so much stuff into the mix that our current consensus is that we need more info. But if you want to get acquainted with the current discussions, here you go:
There exists a wish-granting "machine", otherwise known as "the wishing well", that is capable of connecting people to parallel worlds. Entities, known as "gods", establish a certain symbiosis with humans by granting them access to it (possibility), and are in danger of being thrown to the bottom of the well if not enough humans believe in them.

Said gods can settle in these "willing" vessels (people that made the wish), and more or less feel what they feel. This, in turn, also allows them to create half-"divine" offspring through the host having sex, which are called a sort of rabbit (I forgot the specific term). There are many of these half-divine beings among the girls.

It has been highly suggested that every time the world "resets", it's actually due to a wish being made (that's what Maya Prime seems to have been doing, which she called praying). It is also currently unknown if the world was actually being reset, or that they were all transported into yet another parallel universe - because there has been an instance of them being transported to different kumon-mis during the reset. At the moment it is also unclear if that was time-travel, or dimensional travel (meaning that they could have gone to a past/future of the current kumon-mi, or other kumon-mis entirely.

The fact that Yuu apparently has fathered both Akira/Nozomu with Saki, Sekai with Miu, and Nodoka with Kyoko - could also be explained by each of them being from different realities. We don't know yet.

As for someone being reset, currently it has been suggested that one's memories/self can be stored somewhere else, while a copy takes its place. If that happens to everyone, or just with Maya Prime, is unknown. There is also the possibility that Maya, especially, is a specific cog of the machine meant to accompany Akira. Ami being the previous template to this function, eventually replaced by Maya, and possibly due to being replaced by Nao-chan eventually (whose real name is TEMPLATE9).

Regarding Akira, it has been explained by Nodoka that his abilities are to "slip" his consciousness into other dimensions, which he does effortlessly. She also explains that "slipping" is actually highly difficult, and that others can also slip (including her mom, who slipped and never came back), either through supernatural help (usually with an egg), or through him. These slips can also be physical.

Finally, chapter 4 crushed the mythology of 3 to 4 gods, bringing in an actual infinite amount of them. Pareidolia shifted from Akira to Yumi, even though he was supposed to have been created for Akira. Kaori is home to many gods even if she's unwilling (probably due to parts of her body being from Sekai). Sekai also has been revealed to have been assaulted by the gods during her last year of life. And Sara suffered through the same when she was younger.

Through all of this, an unnamed narrator, probably Himawari, has explained that, ultimately, her wish for a better world is to have a perfect harmony. For every human to have a god, for the gates to be open and friendly - but that it was impossible since "he left". All of this is, honestly, quite messy and doesn't align properly yet (maybe it never will).
Basically, what a mess. I do hope that Selebus can deliver in at least some of this.

Finally, chapter 4 crushed the mythology of 3 to 4 gods, bringing in an actual infinite amount of them. Pareidolia shifted from Akira to Yumi, even though he was supposed to have been created for Akira. Kaori is home to many gods even if she's unwilling (probably due to parts of her body being from Sekai). Sekai also has been revealed to have been assaulted by the gods during her last year of life. And Sara suffered through the same when she was younger.
Through all of this, an unnamed narrator, probably Himawari, has explained that, ultimately, her wish for a better world is to have a perfect harmony. For every human to have a god, for the gates to be open and friendly - but that it was impossible since "he left". All of this is, honestly, quite messy and doesn't align properly yet (maybe it never will).

The benefit is that you won't have sex with her, and the story will make a point of it when it's relevant.
Echoing what fasoaga said, I think you ought to try to get as many events as possible (which we call the green path) because it'll be closer to what the author intended his story to go. Combining the Ami rejection with Sara, Maki and Haruka, you're likely to miss a huge chunk of the story - much of which has nothing to do with sex, but are revelations that need you to be on their paths to unlock.

Also, regarding choice in general, when it's presented to you, it will almost always result in a less coherent and, honestly, inferior storytelling if you ever choose not to have sex with someone. This extends to choosing "not to see something" choices as well. Be sure to follow the walkthrough mod, be courageous in choosing to see everything, and when presented with a "marry, fuck, kill" do not pick "kill" for Kirin - and you should be fine in terms of green path.
Finally, a good thing to spare your conscience is that you're not the protagonist. It's a bit misleading in the beginning, but "Sensei" is his own character. And even choices such as "not having sex with Ami" will eventually become rather pointless in the grand scheme of things. Try to get most of the story is my suggestion.

Depends what you mean by "benefit". It alters the story somewhat and you may enjoy the tone of their relationship more because of that. My "good uncle" run was probably my favourite playthrough, though it wasn't my first.

From a purely practical standpoint - no, there's no benefit. You will miss out on a dozen events (and counting, surely) including a couple of Happy Events (which are obviously very important as far as the lore and story go). Not all of these events involve just Ami and at least one of these events seemingly still happens in the story and you simply don't get to see what happens. If you want the full picture, you need to finger your niece.

In my opinion (and assuming you love the game) LiL is something that should be played at least twice - I started my second playthrough almost immediately after finishing the first and it was every bit as enjoyable for all the foreshadowing and my increased understanding of what was happening, if not more enjoyable. So, my personal recommendation for anyone is to do a green path first and a red second - although now that I'm thinking about it the other way round might be interesting too since your second playthrough would fill in some blanks. If you think you'll only do one playthrough definitely do it though, I'd say

tl;dr finger your niece

Edit: To be clear when I said it "alters the story somewhat" I'm just talking about some dialogue changes here and there since the nature of Ami and Sensei's relationship is different. The direction of the story is completely the same. Just wanna be clear that the actual plot isn't radically different or anything lol

I don't find that too surprising, I think the events the poems are in tend to be what's worth discussing since they're more informing, especially with how short the poems usually are - with some exceptions like 'Good Boy', which was the only bit of information we had for a long time on Sensei's relationship with his brother. I also think Sel tries too hard sometimes to make them artsy and substantive which winds up achieving the opposite, I imagine there's quite a few I can't even remember because I just glaze over them and I'm sure plenty of people here are the same lol

Despite that though yeah, generally speaking I actually like them a lot. The ones I really enjoy tend to be the ones that aren't really substantive or worth discussing, though - like the one through 'Cardinal' (the event where Makoto and Sensei finally kiss) or at the start of 'Transference' (Sensei's first trip to see Yasu at the Church). There's not really much to say about them; they're just simple, relevant poems that work well with the events they're in.

Yeah Redbirds Bleed and Blue Ones Die, I loved that one too. Reminder that all of the poetry in the game is logged on the wiki:
https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=Poetry

One of my favorites is this one
Cicada songs and lemon drops - a shiny coin for choco-pops.
A puddle near that old oak tree - the things that you would do to me.
Play make-believe. Play hide and seek. Play hopscotch during Golden Week.
That hamster wheel we bought last year - a picture book of grazing deer.
And a pile of rocks that does naught but make me wish that I was home.
With tickle-fights and bug-filled nets - we'd stare up at that spring sunset.

...

We used to think so many things. We had so many songs to sing.
But now we rarely open our mouths because our teeth keep dripping onto our candy bars.
Such better days, I miss our youth! I miss all of my time with you!
I miss falling down. Miss bandaged knees. Miss fireflies and centipedes.
Miss the way you looked when you'd look at me. Miss the way I looked when I couldn't see.
I can do that now. All the light's grown in. But my youth is gone, I'm spread too thin.

...
Don't remember it off the top of my head so I had to look it up, but certainly made an impact on me the first time I read it

For me the poem evokes the simple joys of childhood, ones that you latch onto to distract you from the darkness that lurked in your life that you knew existed at the time but you couldn't quite yet understand or come to terms with.

Imo poetry is more about making you feel things rather than telling a story. It's supposed to be vague enough for you to be able to take bits and pieces of it that you can resonate with.

Miss the way you looked when you'd look at me. Miss the way I looked when I couldn't see.
I can do that now. All the light's grown in. But my youth is gone, I'm spread too thin.
