aramaug said:
I quite like "Il Cervo", what exactly do you object to in it?
Click to expand...
I find it obnoxious.
Sure, "Il cervo" could work for the reasons you cite, but that's exactly why it doesn't work for me. No one walks out of that event with the thought that it was a shared experience that didn't actually happen. We only get that from a commentary released months later, which isn't meant to be read as part of the experience of the game, and thus the actual effect is keeping the player playing the idiot trying to figure the event out when it's actually meant to be nothing. Selebus states that it was fucking random imagery that he thought of on the spot while trying to convey "feelings".

No whale, no deer, no Kaori and no Akira. There was no game, there were no stories, they weren't even there. Only Selebus spouting whatever crap he thinks on the spot and abusing the trust agreement (in terms of time investment) between author and reader in the worst way possible. To me, "Il cervo" is insulting to the audience.

To actually make it into what you said, I think there either should be a signal that it didn't happen inside the game, like Akira talking to Ami or Kaori about the game and they don't remember it - or make into an explicit happy event (which resolves the issue of the audience taking it as something that is actually happening).

Furthermore, "Il cervo" is a monument of the much bigger problem with LiL right now (imo) in that I really question just how much time I'll even spend thinking about its "mysteries" - because, in the end, a lot of it has been nearing bullshit territory. A lot of us have taken to interpreting LiL as a mystery to be solved as a community, when Selebus has dedicated a lot of this chapter to showing how it isn't that much of a puzzle at all. It is rather about a painter figuring how to portray the exact same motif in different and experimentative ways each month while managing to not touch on the actual very small percertage of it that he has thought through long-term.

I tire of the god of the week, the mythology pulled out of the ass each month that contradicts what has been shown before (and yet it doesn't because make believe has conveniently been made canon in the universe), the running around in a circle and creating more stuff, instead of actually explaining what has been mentioned before - and then, when he does, it barely fits anyway.

Who is the old one? What the hell is buried underneath his feet? Why is it important that Akira carries a picture of Ami in his pocket? Fuck it, what about the fireside ghost stories from Futaba and Nodoka? I tire of the way Selebus does things. Nothing is ever clear, even when he does reveal something. He pokes fun at people never moving on from "the letter T", and yet is his own fault for not being able to follow-up with payoff for his "revelations", instead of just throwing them around in the midst of yet another bundle of gods of clowns, holes, scissors and plants.
To me, "Il cervo" is a flag that reminds me that, quite unfortunately, thinking too much about this game is fruitless. And the measure for what "too much" is is currently getting lower and lower.

I have lost faith that spending time thinking about what Selebus is trying to convey is going to better my experience, rather, ignoring some amount of what he says is currently doing that instead. None of this, while wordy, should come at any surprise though, I've been vocal on how I've been rather disappointed with LiL lately.

We only get that from a commentary released months later, which isn't meant to be read as part of the experience of the game, and thus the actual effect is keeping the player playing the idiot trying to figure the event out when it's actually meant to be nothing. Selebus states that it was fucking random imagery that he thought of on the spot while trying to convey "feelings".
No whale, no deer, no Kaori and no Akira. There was no game, there were no stories, they weren't even there. Only Selebus spouting whatever crap he thinks on the spot and abusing the trust agreement (in terms of time investment) between author and reader in the worst way possible. To me, "Il cervo" is insulting to the audience.
To actually make it into what you said, I think there either should be a signal that it didn't happen
inside
the game, like Akira talking to Ami or Kaori about the game and they don't remember it - or make into an explicit happy event (which resolves the issue of the audience taking it as something that is actually happening).
Furthermore, "Il cervo" is a monument of the much bigger problem with LiL right now (imo) in that I really question just how much time I'll even spend thinking about its "mysteries" - because, in the end, a lot of it has been nearing bullshit territory. A lot of us have taken to interpreting LiL as a mystery to be solved as a community, when Selebus has dedicated a lot of this chapter to showing how it isn't that much of a puzzle at all. It is rather about a painter figuring how to portray the exact same motif in different and experimentative ways each month while managing to not touch on the actual very small percertage of it that he has thought through long-term.
I tire of the god of the week, the mythology pulled out of the ass each month that contradicts what has been shown before (and yet it doesn't because make believe has conveniently been made canon in the universe), the running around in a circle and creating more stuff, instead of actually explaining what has been mentioned before - and then, when he does, it barely fits anyway.
Who is the old one? What the hell is buried underneath his feet? Why is it important that Akira carries a picture of Ami in his pocket? Fuck it, what about the fireside ghost stories from Futaba and Nodoka? I tire of the way Selebus does things. Nothing is ever clear, even when he does reveal something. He pokes fun at people never moving on from "the letter T", and yet is his own fault for not being able to follow-up with payoff for his "revelations", instead of just throwing them around in the midst of yet another bundle of gods of clowns, holes, scissors and plants.

We only get that from a commentary released months later, which isn't meant to be read as part of the experience of the game, and thus the actual effect is keeping the player playing the idiot trying to figure the event out when it's actually meant to be nothing. Selebus states that it was fucking random imagery that he thought of on the spot while trying to convey "feelings".

No whale, no deer, no Kaori and no Akira. There was no game, there were no stories, they weren't even there. Only Selebus spouting whatever crap he thinks on the spot and abusing the trust agreement (in terms of time investment) between author and reader in the worst way possible. To me, "Il cervo" is insulting to the audience.

To actually make it into what you said, I think there either should be a signal that it didn't happen inside the game, like Akira talking to Ami or Kaori about the game and they don't remember it - or make into an explicit happy event (which resolves the issue of the audience taking it as something that is actually happening).

Furthermore, "Il cervo" is a monument of the much bigger problem with LiL right now (imo) in that I really question just how much time I'll even spend thinking about its "mysteries" - because, in the end, a lot of it has been nearing bullshit territory. A lot of us have taken to interpreting LiL as a mystery to be solved as a community, when Selebus has dedicated a lot of this chapter to showing how it isn't that much of a puzzle at all. It is rather about a painter figuring how to portray the exact same motif in different and experimentative ways each month while managing to not touch on the actual very small percertage of it that he has thought through long-term.

I tire of the god of the week, the mythology pulled out of the ass each month that contradicts what has been shown before (and yet it doesn't because make believe has conveniently been made canon in the universe), the running around in a circle and creating more stuff, instead of actually explaining what has been mentioned before - and then, when he does, it barely fits anyway.

Who is the old one? What the hell is buried underneath his feet? Why is it important that Akira carries a picture of Ami in his pocket? Fuck it, what about the fireside ghost stories from Futaba and Nodoka? I tire of the way Selebus does things. Nothing is ever clear, even when he does reveal something. He pokes fun at people never moving on from "the letter T", and yet is his own fault for not being able to follow-up with payoff for his "revelations", instead of just throwing them around in the midst of yet another bundle of gods of clowns, holes, scissors and plants.
To me, "Il cervo" is a flag that reminds me that, quite unfortunately, thinking too much about this game is fruitless. And the measure for what "too much" is is currently getting lower and lower.

I have lost faith that spending time thinking about what Selebus is trying to convey is going to better my experience, rather, ignoring some amount of what he says is currently doing that instead. None of this, while wordy, should come at any surprise though, I've been vocal on how I've been rather dissapointed with LiL lately.
Click to expand...
I guess we have a fundamental difference of opinion. I have problems with some of the current direction of the main plot (though a lot of it is still very good), with character arcs that I think he bungled and the misplaced focus on Sensei's own development despite its glacial pacing, but my enjoyment of the metaplot and the mysteries hasn't diminished at all.

It's frustrating to not have specific questions answered because we're curious and we want to know now, but I don't think it becomes a writing failure until it's clear that the writer doesn't have any satisfactory answers. In any case, while we might not be getting the exact answers we want, we are still constantly learning other things. At times it feels like Selebus is stringing us along (I'm thinking about things like the boxes or Maya and Noriko's history), but I've never felt that he's stalling while he makes shit up as he goes. I think he's just had a specific pacing of reveals in mind from the start.

I doubt I'm going to convince you on "Il Cervo" but I still think it's worth trying to get across my point of view.
Sure, "Il cervo" could work for the reasons you cite, but that's exactly why it doesn't work for me. No one walks out of that event with the thought that it was a shared experience that didn't actually happen. We only get that from a commentary released months later
Click to expand...
My point was that the things that I like in the event work if it's real and also work if it isn't. Before the commentary I didn't interpret it as a shared dream, but I think that just adds additional context rather than drastically changing the way I view the event.

I will say that even before reading the commentary I thought it had a clear feeling of unreality. Stuff like the eerie/uncanny music (previously used for all sorts of surreal stuff in the church and a bus ride backward that was just a "dream"), visual oddities like the camp chairs suddenly disappearing, the way the characters talk past each other as much as to each other, and how they casually accept surreal aspects like the bizarre rules of the game. I still thought the characters were physically around the fire, but at the very least Sensei's mind was going haywire and something similar was happening to Ami and Kaori.
No whale, no deer, no Kaori and no Akira. There was no game, there were no stories, they weren't even there. Only Selebus spouting whatever crap he thinks on the spot
Click to expand...
I just don't agree with this, the stories are real whether they were physically there to tell them or not. Using symbols to convey atmosphere or feeling is still valid even if they don't have a literal meaning (though I also think the whale and deer parts stories contain a lot of literal meaning regarding the metaplot).
To actually make it into what you said, I think there either should be a signal that it didn't happen inside the game, like Akira talking to Ami or Kaori about the game and they don't remember it
Click to expand...
If the commentary is to be believed, they probably would remember it just as much as Sensei since it was still a shared experience.

Ultimately I don't think it matters though, just like it doesn't matter if the event is "real" or not. This is a completely self-contained conversation that reaches no conclusion. The characters aren't swayed by each other's words and they don't have any sort of revelation. If they forget the event it won't change anything, because the event wasn't about things the characters learned; it was about things shown to the reader.

I guess while I’m already making a post, I may as well talk about this upcoming update real quick.

Man, this one is kinda difficult to gauge, even with the previews we’ve gotten…

From the looks of things, Tsubasa, Kaori and Nao will likely be the stars of the show here if we’re to get anything meaningful that sets up for the Beach two-parter. Maybe we’ll even learn a bit more about Ami and her current motivations during Wakana’s conversation with her. Who knows…

But wow… I want to look at this changelog:

3 Nao-chan events, 2 Chinami events, 2 Tsukasa events… It really is the ‘Wizard Update’, huh?

Speaking of which… let’s address the elephant in the room: “Will any Wizard get an h-scene this update? Will Akira finally cross that horrendous and forbidden line before shit hits the fan with the gods again at the Beach?”

It’s hard to say obviously… especially when some speculate this will be a mostly filler update once again. However, I have a sneaking suspicion that it will…

Akira’s been insanely self-destructive as of late, and I have a feeling that it will continue. After all, how much lower can you possibly sink than that? The dude’s not only an addict, but also seemingly wants consequences for his actions because that’s the only way he believes he can stop himself.

…Which Wizard would it be if it happens, though?

Nao-chan? Doubtful. I believe her role in this update will be strictly lore related with the looks we’ve gotten at her previews, which are a callback to the very first events of the whole game: “Every Day I Grow Some More” and “A New You”. What significance that will have? We shall see.

Chinami? It’s… possible I guess, but I’m still gonna say I don’t think so. Chika is literally there in the previews and I don’t sense anything ominous about any of them or Chinami’s event titles.

I mean… unless Chika has completely flown off the deep end and does a complete 180 on her protectiveness of Chinami. Didn’t she spend her entire TSS event sacrificing her own wellbeing so that Chinami would be protected? I feel like Chika, even as much as she’s changed, still has limits when it comes to her sister.

Which only leaves…

Tsukasa.

I’m kinda worried for her, y’all.

Remember Christmas at the Tsukioka Manor? How Tsubasa pushed her away even further? How Akira continued to successfully groom her on the Green Path? Tsukasa is even (supposedly) watching internet porn with Chinami in one of the previews, probably out of curiosity more than anything.

…Sure would be ironic if that ‘learning material’ became useful later in the very same update.

I’m not gonna say full on penetration will happen, because I mean… we saw how things went for Miku. But at the very least, I feel like something unsavory will happen with Tsukasa.

But yes… as sad as it is to say, who does Tsukasa even have as an adult figure in her life? The father who neglects her? The mother who constantly reminds her that she isn’t the favorite? That she’s disposable?

Akira has paid attention to her, though… At least moreso in comparison to her parents. And that, sadly, is why Tsukasa will latch onto him. Because she has no one else who fills that role.

It’s all part of Tsubasa’s plan too… or… I guess the Whispers of the World’s plan? Still don’t know what that was all about, but yeah.

…On a slightly different note, if all this speculation turns out to be bullshit, then I’d say Touka has a pretty good chance! So that’s something, right?

Personally though, I’m far more curious about what will happen at the Beach… I’ve noticed that the Beach was a key location for some actual answers ever since the last Reset, and have no doubt that another one is on its way.

If the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad (the one that was at the Beach during “Perfect Harmony”) doesn’t get their memories back after this next Reset Puzzle, that would honestly kinda piss me off lol. Because at this point, I’d say we’ve earned the right to see things finally progress plot-wise.

I’m going into it with an open mind. Sel’s writing has definitely gotten weird asf lately, but I really want to give him the benefit of the doubt that this is all leading somewhere.

Nao-chan? Doubtful. I believe her role in this update will be strictly lore related with the looks we’ve gotten at her previews, which are a callback to the very first events of the whole game: “Every Day I Grow Some More” and “A New You”. What significance that will have? We shall see.

Chinami? It’s… possible I guess, but I’m still gonna say I don’t think so. Chika is literally there in the previews and I don’t sense anything ominous about any of them or Chinami’s event titles.

I mean… unless Chika has completely flown off the deep end and does a complete 180 on her protectiveness of Chinami. Didn’t she spend her entire TSS event sacrificing her own wellbeing so that Chinami would be protected? I feel like Chika, even as much as she’s changed, still has limits when it comes to her sister.

Which only leaves…

Tsukasa.

I’m kinda worried for her, y’all.

Remember Christmas at the Tsukioka Manor? How Tsubasa pushed her away even further? How Akira continued to successfully groom her on the Green Path? Tsukasa is even (supposedly) watching internet porn with Chinami in one of the previews, probably out of curiosity more than anything.

I’m not gonna say full on penetration will happen, because I mean… we saw how things went for Miku. But at the very least, I feel like something unsavory will happen with Tsukasa.

But yes… as sad as it is to say, who does Tsukasa even have as an adult figure in her life? The father who neglects her? The mother who constantly reminds her that she isn’t the favorite? That she’s disposable?

Akira has paid attention to her, though… At least moreso in comparison to her parents. And that, sadly, is why Tsukasa will latch onto him. Because she has no one else who fills that role.

It’s all part of Tsubasa’s plan too… or… I guess the Whispers of the World’s plan? Still don’t know what that was all about, but yeah.

…On a slightly different note, if all this speculation turns out to be bullshit, then I’d say Touka has a pretty good chance! So that’s something, right?

Personally though, I’m far more curious about what will happen at the Beach… I’ve noticed that the Beach was a key location for some actual answers ever since the last Reset, and have no doubt that another one is on its way.

If the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad (the one that was at the Beach during “Perfect Harmony”) doesn’t get their memories back after this next Reset Puzzle, that would honestly kinda piss me off lol. Because at this point, I’d say we’ve earned the right to see things finally progress plot-wise.

I’m going into it with an open mind. Sel’s writing has definitely gotten weird asf lately, but I really want to give him the benefit of the doubt that this is all leading somewhere.

platinumgoose said:
Sometimes when I read the thread I feel strange. I like the story Selebus writes, also Chapter 4. Many here seem not to enjoy, but they still read, and talk about how bad things are now.
Click to expand...
Please take a moment to look at the following:


Almost every single one of these messages have been in this thread, and almost every single one of these reactions to the messages have been on posts more or less praising the game, be it tacitly by delving into the lore, geeking out on stuff, or interacting with the community around the game.
If you've been feeling strange by reading the thread because we're negative, you haven't been reading it long. Here's a new and (imo) accurate way of looking at the "negativity": We're supporting eachother through this, it's a support group. There have been elements, for months now, that we don't like and by sharing it with others, and feeling validated, we can move past it and try to focus on the aspects of the game that we still like.

Also, I don't like this idea of "if you don't enjoy it, why read it and talk about how bad it is?" - as many have pointed out, we didn't pick up LiL last month and can simply drop the story no strings attached. There's a lot of us invested in it and in this community. Would I drop it if the story turned into complete shit? It's likely. But we're not there by a long shot.

If you feel like you'd rather be in the company of a strictly "positive" reaction to LiL, there's always the discord. You won't find anyone having the slighest complaint about anything there (for long).

Also, I don't like this idea of "if you don't enjoy it, why read it and talk about how bad it is?" - as many have pointed out, we didn't pick up LiL last month and can simply drop the story no strings attached. There's a lot of us invested in it and in this community. Would I drop it if the story turned into complete shit? It's likely. But we're not there by a long shot.
If you feel like you'd rather be in the company of a strictly "positive" reaction to LiL, there's always the discord. You won't find anyone having the slighest complaint about anything there (for long).

Nao-chan? Doubtful. I believe her role in this update will be strictly lore related with the looks we’ve gotten at her previews, which are a callback to the very first events of the whole game: “Every Day I Grow Some More” and “A New You”. What significance that will have? We shall see.

Chinami? It’s… possible I guess, but I’m still gonna say I don’t think so. Chika is literally there in the previews and I don’t sense anything ominous about any of them or Chinami’s event titles.

I mean… unless Chika has completely flown off the deep end and does a complete 180 on her protectiveness of Chinami. Didn’t she spend her entire TSS event sacrificing her own wellbeing so that Chinami would be protected? I feel like Chika, even as much as she’s changed, still has limits when it comes to her sister.

Which only leaves…

Tsukasa.

I’m kinda worried for her, y’all.

Remember Christmas at the Tsukioka Manor? How Tsubasa pushed her away even further? How Akira continued to successfully groom her on the Green Path? Tsukasa is even (supposedly) watching internet porn with Chinami in one of the previews, probably out of curiosity more than anything.

…Sure would be ironic if that ‘learning material’ became useful later in the very same update.

I’m not gonna say full on penetration will happen, because I mean… we saw how things went for Miku. But at the very least, I feel like something unsavory will happen with Tsukasa.

But yes… as sad as it is to say, who does Tsukasa even have as an adult figure in her life? The father who neglects her? The mother who constantly reminds her that she isn’t the favorite? That she’s disposable?

Akira has paid attention to her, though… At least moreso in comparison to her parents. And that, sadly, is why Tsukasa will latch onto him. Because she has no one else who fills that role.

It’s all part of Tsubasa’s plan too… or… I guess the Whispers of the World’s plan? Still don’t know what that was all about, but yeah.

…On a slightly different note, if all this speculation turns out to be bullshit, then I’d say Touka has a pretty good chance! So that’s something, right?

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
Please take a moment to look at the following:
View attachment 5098367

Almost every single one of these messages have been in this thread, and almost every single one of these reactions to the messages have been on posts more or less praising the game, be it tacitly by delving into the lore, geeking out on stuff, or interacting with the community around the game.
If you've been feeling strange by reading the thread because we're negative, you haven't been reading it long. Here's a new and (imo) accurate way of looking at the "negativity": We're supporting eachother through this, it's a support group. There have been elements, for months now, that we don't like and by sharing it with others, and feeling validated, we can move past it and try to focus on the aspects of the game that we still like.

Also, I don't like this idea of "if you don't enjoy it, why read it and talk about how bad it is?" - as many have pointed out, we didn't pick up LiL last month and can simply drop the story no strings attached. There's a lot of us invested in it and in this community. Would I drop it if the story turned into complete shit? It's likely. But we're not there by a long shot.

If you feel like you'd rather be in the company of a strictly "positive" reaction to LiL, there's always the discord. You won't find anyone having the slighest complaint about anything there (for long).
Click to expand...
I think I explained my feelings unwell. I feel strange because I feel like maybe I am wrong.
Sometimes it is difficult to understand so for a long time reading from everyone here helped me to understand many complicated things in the story. In Chapter 3 people were very excited for things to happen, but now people are more disappointed. Since I am happy I wonder if maybe I missed things that others see when I like things others who helped me to understand are unhappy with. I don't want you to not speak if you are unhappy.

03 - Makoto 1 (linked)

16 - Kaori 3 (linked)

Karin


Savefile for 0.51
*Walkthrough mod is needed.
**Green Route means that this is a save in which there is no missed event, aka Akira has done everything he possibly could.
***Every stat (Love/Lust/Headpats) has been bumped to an amount that would get you through any requirements automatically (restricted to the ones that have been unlocked for grinding). All unlockables (outfits) are also unlocked, as are the bonus scenes.
Renpy saves in two separate locations. First one is the easiest. Either go to:

1. locate your game directory (wherever you installed it), the structure should be "lessons in love (or whatever you named it)">"game">"saves". Just drop the file there.

2. Locate your system drive, the structure should be "C: (it's usually C)" > "Users" > "your user name" > "AppData" > "Roaming" > "Renpy" > "Test 2 (this is the name Selebus gave LessonsInLove in the registry)". Drop the file there.

Now, the name of the file dictates in what page it will be. If it's "1-1-LT1", it will be the first page, in the first spot. If it's "9-6-LT1", it will be the 9th page, in the 6th spot.


Edit: Tsubasa's chain is likely bugged on the red path, we will have to wait for the next update to be sure. If you'd like to view the events, simply download the savefile for the green path until then.

Okay now I'm starting to wonder some things about Tsubasa

It's already pretty apparent that she knows more about the mechanics of the world that she lets on, with her secret meeting and plans with Himawari in a prior update, CONSTANT vague allusions to her possibly having knowledge of the loops, and even being the narrator to certain events in the game.



Sensei: "Not Really."

Tsubasa: "Hahaha! Not yet, you mean."


I could be reaching a bit here, but the more I read of her lines the more difficult I feel I can take them at face value.
This could be taken as simple flirting, but it's possible shes alluding that it's bound to happen...Like she's experienced it before or has some sort of knowledge of the future.

Anyways, continuing with the limo scene in 0.43. After making references to Sekai herself ("What's wrong, Aki-kun? Cat got your tongue?") and vague discussons of fate, the conversation shifts to sex.

Tsubasa: The craziest thing I've ever done? Has there been anything like that?


Not only does she imply the story is fabricated by reusing the same scene in a different context, but the scene itself also looks remarkably familiar does it not?


I mean it's almost identical, as if she's specifically referencing what happened to her "old friend" she mentions in the very same conversation right beforehand.


But wait, how would she be referencing an event that hasn't even happened yet? Unless... she has either seen it happen before in a separate reset, or has some sort of foresight.


The way this is stated it's almost like this is a well-known trait that she's familiar with by now. Plus, she wasn't even present (this time?) so how would she even know how much of a fight Yuki put up? Sure, we could just write it off as her somehow having camera footage, corporate espionage with her endless connections, etc. But is that really it? Is is just as simple as Tsubasa has so many connections that she sees everything going on in Kumon-mi and is a bonafide stalker?

This could also help to explain how she ends up arriving at the perfect time right after this particular traumatic event plays out. Seemingly out of nowhere like some sort of deus ex machina... So convenient as a matter of fact it makes one think she knew it was going to happen.

The thing I don't know is why she wouldn't try to stop it from happening. Perhaps she knows it's going to happen but can't stop it, maybe she's attempted to in the past and always fails or can't mess with the "fate" too much without consequences. We still don't know the full extent of her and Himawari's cooperation and plans and if this is part of it or not. Admittedly these are weak explanations, but it gets me thinking...

TL;DR, I question her "stories" about her getting gangbanged before marriage/by the massage staff because she contradicts them with statements like "the staff would never dare touch her even if she wanted them to", acting as if her sexual knowledge is lacking during the impromtu family sexual ed course, and even says that she's never even been nude in front of anyone during the Yuki flashback. Which could still be before she was married, but the whole idea is such an outlandish claim to begin with especially when she prefaces her answer with "Has there been anything like that?"
Plus the scenes she conjures up when talking about it eerily mirrors the scene of Yuki getting gangbanged, in which she miraculously appears to the rescue right after it happens.

posts.content_html_raw:
I enjoyed the update, though nothing really wowed me the way multiple events in 0.48 and 0.46 did. The highlight was definitely the humor, with this update having some of the funniest events in recent memory (Wakana & Akira, Chinami & Tsukasa, everything involving Nao).
- Yumi caring about her family (and trying to pretend she doesn't) is very cute.

- Both Wakana scenes were good, and it's nice to see an actually competent adult try to help in a way that won't overwhelm the Arakawas. I'm a little disappointed we didn't get more out of her scene with Ami, though. It seems like her time obsessing over The Girl Who Cannot Breathe should have resulted in more than just knowing she molested Akira.

- I don't think it was actually Karin who texted Sensei, but instead Kirin pretending to be her to try to get them to talk at the beach.
Doesn't show herself in the picture, pointedly avoids letting Sensei hear her voice:

Isn't sure what Karin did or didn't say previously:

Wants to talk to Sensei but won't do it "herself":

- Sensei balks at Makoto's plan that might reset "meat puppet" Maya, but last chapter he went along with Maya Prime's pregnancy experiment despite the risk he could lose the "real" Ayane. This guy really has some fucked-up priorities (not that that's news to anyone).

- I'm glad to see the (long-overdue) return of Futaba's storyline as an aspiring writer. Those events were when she was the most interesting as a character.

- Chinami shows a great deal of insight for someone her age, but in some things she's just hopelessly naive (thinking it would help Tsukasa to have Sensei "teach" her), which makes a lot of sense for a precocious kid with such limited experience of the world.

- I wasn't a big fan of the Tsukioka manor scenes, the sitcom vibes were too at odds with the gravity of the subject matter (Tsukasa's sexual "instruction"). I was glad to see Touka stand up to Tsubasa and question her motives, even if it didn't lead to any answers. I was not happy about the way she just moved past the knowledge that Sensei intentionally had sex in front of Tsukasa and has a very creepy attraction to her. People seem way too willing to make the leap from "he preys on high schoolers" to "he wants to do the same to preteens" (Osako does something similar later in the update with regards to Nao).

- Apparently Tsubasa was in love with Yuki and still is, which is cute but also somewhat tragic since Yuki is straight. It helps explain why she (supposedly) wants to let her daughters make their own choices - she wishes she could have abandoned her arranged marriage and been with Yuki instead, but that was never an option for her. I wonder if Tsubasa is also falling for Sensei the way everyone else does or if her special circumstances make her immune to that.

- Yuki and Tsubasa used to have a third close friend, who is implied to be dead now. The most obvious candidates are Sekai or Chiaki; I lean toward Sekai because of the reference to the moon.

...
Conveniently, we're also given an excuse for how Yuki could have known Sekai (or Chiaki) and not pointed out a resemblance in Ami (or Chika). She knew Tsubasa's daughter was in Yumi's class but never said anything because she apparently wanted to forget that part of her life.

- Nao is the best.

She should show that last one to Ami, it would be a great bonding experience.

I also loved the way she casually swatted away SeKaori.

- Green is now Kaori's favorite color; previously she said it was her biggest fear (in Chapter 3). That change could indicate that she's moving away from Pareidolia and back toward Wires, despite SeKaori's greater activity.

- It would appear that Himawari is the PA Voice from the TSS events, which means she also narrated Sana's (at least).
This again points to her having a "day job" working for the gods, but she's going behind their backs to work with Tsubasa on her own plans.

- Not for the first time, it stuck out to me that SeKaori's personality is completely different from either Ghost Sekai or the one from Sensei's memories. She lacks their sense of playfulness, the way they constantly tease Akira and refuse to take anything seriously. This time she did sound a lot like someone else, though: Pareidolia. I'm going to need to think on this some more.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just finished the update and took like 5 minutes to process it before I started typing this. I have quite a bit to say while it's still fresh on my mind, so I guess I'll get into it.

General Thoughts: I really enjoyed this one! It wasn't nearly as depressing as the last update was. For the most part, it was definitely set-up for the upcoming Beach Reset, but we did get some interesting moments here, especially with Nao-chan. More on that later.

I'm glad that the two of them can finally have a real discussion and get some semblance of closure on their issues... even if they still have a long way to go. Oh, and Yumi finally got that 10K! Didn't really expect that to ever get referenced again, but hey! Good for her.

I'm sooo glad that Makoto is taking a more active role and is pitching ideas for what they can do about the time loops, even if she clearly doesn't want to actually do anything about them. I'm also glad she brought up the possibility that the rooftop may not even be necessary to carry memories over, because if and when a Reset does occur at the Beach, they may not have a choice about fleeing to the Rooftop or not.

What'll they do? Take a bus, limo or some other vehicle back to the school while Sensei and everyone else are either gone or tripping balls? Doubtful.

I'm very intrigued to see how that's gonna play out...

Also, don't you lie, Rin. You were totally jealous. (Side note: I'm so glad her hair is back to normal.)

Uh huh... Uh huh... Futaba's back to writing stories to boost her self-esteem, we get verbal confirmation once again that her parents are still missing... all seems as expected here-

What the fuck!?



You mean to tell me there are cameras watching Kumon-mi's every move? HimawariCo ones at that?? That- That... kind of explains a lot, actually. How the simulation is being monitored (assuming you even subscribe to that theory) or perhaps the entire game is a TV show for someone or something's entertainment.

It's kind of like Makoto's analogy about the ant farm... or how Nao (not Nao-chan) basically alluded to the same exact thing during "Mother's Milk"... Not to mention the Untitled Children's Show is a thing that exists too...

Yeahhhh... I think 'cosmic TV show' is the theory I'm leaning towards right now as far as what the hell is going on in general. Perhaps the simulation theory can still work if you combine elements from both, though.

Regardless, we know that Kumon-mi is being monitored. That's for certain. This isn't the last time we hear about HimawariCo in the update either.

Her event was alright. I'm sure the Miku fans out there are happy she can get another shot at lewd content that isn't orchestrated by Nodoka, but tbh, this was more for the fan service. I like the sex scenes in this game, but really, it's secondary to everything else that's going on.

That conversation was way less chaotic than I expected... With Akira and Ami both, really. But mostly Ami. Kind of interesting that Ami would feel more comfortable with Wakana in the mother role at her house than Niki, but I suppose it makes some amount of sense. Unless Ami was just out to fluster and confuse Wakana to escape the conversation... That would be a total Arakawa thing to do.

I really don't know what to say about Ami this time. We didn't get a whole lot, but... maybe she'll try and talk with Akira during the Beach Trip? I don't see why she wouldn't. A Reset is the perfect time to see more of Ami and her motivations. Guess we'll see.

Talk about cuckoo for Cocoa Puffs, amirite?

Lol nah but seriously, what a sad fucking situation... She's still stuck on this idea that Sensei loves her the most. And I suppose in his own warped way, he does love her like he loves so many other girls. But it's just... not sustainable, and it's a downright tragedy to see how much she's changed since Chapter 1. What friends does she even have now? I mean, I suppose Rin at this point and that's it.

Yumi has been distant ever since Chika got rabies and has buddied up more to Noriko by now, and... I dunno, can you call her Maid Cafe co-workers friends of hers? They're friendly, sure (except for Ami), but they aren't like... actual close friends. Which tbh, she needs more than ever. It doesn't just affect her, but it affects Chinami too, which we can evidently see throughout both of their events.

I truly hope she improves at some point, man, but I don't see it happening anytime soon unless Reset shenanigans happen or something.

...On a brighter note, Chika's two h-scenes were pretty hot tho. As per usual. I also see Chika has done her hair up in a ponytail like she did in Chapter 1. Made me a little nostalgic. I like it. I like Yuki's new hairstyle too. And Osako's. And Noriko's.

Wow... so many good new hairstyle choices lately.

...Yeah, not gonna lie, this one was emotional. Any event involving Tsukasa is lately. I really do have a soft spot for her character and also the other Wizards.

Seriously though, just look at this response from Chinami after she finds out about Tsukasa's arranged marriage:



Their friendship is so pure, man...

Well, if you ignore the fact they were watching porn together just seconds earlier. But still, you get the idea.

Speaking more on Chinami, it seems she's the next (and last) Wizard in line to watch Akira fuck another girl in front of them. The Wizards' curiosity is now set in motion. All we can do now is... see where it all will lead.



Ugh, goddamn... That longing and vulnerable look in her eyes. Can we protect Tsukasa at all costs please? Thank you.

...Huh. It didn't really click for me until I saw these lines, but... it makes a lot of sense to see why Akira took Wizard Maya under his wing the same way Sekai did. It was his own way of paying things forward. I didn't think about such a thing at first, but yeah, that tracks...

Looks like I was wrong about Tsukasa getting a lewd scene this update, but hey... many things were at the very least set up. It's only a matter of time.



Yuki looks very cute tho...



The only unfortunate part about this is we didn't get to see it ourselves... Now if only the same could be done to Yumi's father, we'd be good.


(When talking about swimming nude in the lake ^)


This is... definitely not something I saw coming at all. Like, if you'd predicted something like Tsubasa crushing on Yuki even a few updates ago, I'd be like 'no way'. But here we are...

It's Selebus after all, and he just looooves his yuri and/or bisexual female characters. But... I dunno, man. I don't really mind this. It makes sense if you remember this is Tsubasa being herself around Yuki, someone she was able to be wild and free with years ago. Only, she had to give that freedom up in exchange for obligation...

I think it's even kinda cute to see Tsubasa this way. All we know her as is this... cold and calculating person, but really, it's evident that she was forced into this divine bullshit the same as the other major players. She's clearly trying to disrupt the world somehow, kind of like Nodoka was trying to do. Only, Tsubasa knows way more than Nodoka could ever hope to thanks to her experience.

Oh yeah... Can we also address that line from Tsubasa where she mentions wishing her and Yuki's "third" was there? Who does she mean? Akira? Sekai maybe? It would certainly explain why she apparently vowed to ‘protect Akira’. So many questions…

In any case, Tsubasa is easily one of the most interesting characters to watch these days by far.

I also wish we got to see Yuki's conversation with Sara, but it happened off-screen unfortunately, so oh well.



Pft... 'Douchefriend'. Yeah, that sums Akira up, alright.

...Huh. It seems The Old One is back for another appearance. What even is the significance of this thing? It's still very creepy looking, whatever it is... and it sure loves following Akira around.

I didn't expect that callback to the Waiting Room Reset Puzzle, but- oh look. Another reference to HimawariCo. What the heck is their deal, even...

Oh yeah, and it also turns out Nao-chan's abilities only get better:


*Snaps fingers*


She can instantly snap Akira out of blackouts (literally).

I know it may seem foolish to trust her and her existence completely, but I meannnn... I dunno. She seems like she'd be a really helpful ally for figuring these time loops out.

My only concern, though... is that it was Wires who had the map sent to Kaori's house originally which led to Nao-chan's discovery. Not only that, but he was responsible for the second map too, which led to that weird ass door in the middle of the woods on the Camping Trip.

What is Wires' end goal here? Is Nao-chan an agent of his, or is she truly just a rogue free agent? There are still many missing pieces to this puzzle...

Kaori continues to be Kaori! Only this time... she actually talks to Yumi at length! (Seriously, how did it take so long for this to happen?) Sekai continues to live in Kaori's (and Akira's) head rent free. No surprise there... It's really sad to see Kaori lose control of herself, especially now that we know what the gods are doing to her.



Sounds familiar, huh... A lot like the last year of Sekai's life, where her mind wasn't her own anymore and she felt unsafe unless Akira was around to help her calm down.

You can really see the desperation in Kaori's eyes too. She doesn't want Akira to get fed up with her and abandon her. After all, she doesn't have many friends to go around.

...Man, she needs a hug too.

Also, wow. Can I just say that there have been so many moments this update where Akira's morals in regards to the Wizards were tested?

"Hey, Papa. Chinami wants to talk about sexual stuff."
"Akira, you need to continue your lessons with Tsukasa and talk with her about sex."
"Wow, Friend! What great mating! Okay, now it's Nao-chan's turn!"

Knowing Sensei, he can only hold that back for so long... This timebomb will be an explosive one once it goes off.



Oh dayum... Kaori's kinkiness knows no bounds.




Okay, so this one is interesting... because like, once Akira picks Nao up from Wakana and Osako's place, they talk alone in Kaori's apartment. And after a surprisingly insightful conversation, Akira says, "it'll take a miracle to figure out this world" or something along those lines. And Nao-chan's response?

"I will be your miracle."

Which brings us to this event, and... wow. I'm glad I decided to save this event for last, because... this one left me with lots to think about. (BTW, major props to Moonflare for the trigger guide as always.)

So Maya starts out masturbating in her room, right? Pretty hot stuff. Then she gets a knock on her door, thinking it to be Sensei, but nope! Surprise! It's Nao-chan. Pretty weird and jarring right off the bat, but then the weird shit happens.

Everything glitches out when the dorm room door opens, then even Moyo and Maya 2 show up. Maya gets pushed into the strange abyss and...

Suddenly we're right back at the first event of the entire game: "Every Day I Grow Some More". Only it's not Sensei this time, it's Maya in his place. And Nao-chan is Ami and Akira is Maya, and... yeah, it's pretty crazy. It almost feels like a Maya TSS event, even though it technically isn't one by name.

The entire goal of this is for Nao to get Maya on the correct path again so that maybe she can regain her memories as Maya Prime, or perhaps even become an even better Maya by the end of it all. Maya doesn't seem to get it, but at the very least, this should get Maya thinking. And perfect timing too! Right before the Beach two-parter.

When Nao said to Akira that she would be 'his miracle', I interpreted this as her saying that she'd help him get Maya Prime back in some capacity so that he can find hope and courage of some kind again. Who knows how effective this will have turned out... Maybe next month we'll get some sort of idea.



Yes. Yes he does.

Okay, so I can't show Maya's because F95's image limit got lowered for whatever reason, but all I'll say about it is it was very nice to look at. It's cool to see Maya finally send a text after all this time. Karin too, whose conversation I found way more interesting.

And speaking of that...



Oh look! It's that same damn cat again. We truly can't escape him, can we?

Anyway, this message only has one real conversation to it, and it seems to be Karin trying to make conversation with Akira again. She essentially confirms that she'll be at the Beach with everyone else and asks him to approach her on his own, which can only mean we'll see this arc continue very soon. I very much look forward to it, because I for one love Karin and where her story's headed.

Closing thoughts: Once again, I felt that this was a solid update. There was a lot of set-up for the Beach for sure, but there were still some very interesting things revealed. Nao-chan was undoubtedly the MVP of this entire update, leaving us with many lingering questions before the long anticipated 8th Reset...

We're in for another wild ride... I just know it. It's almost evil that Sel is taking his vacation right in between those two parts. The inevitable cliffhanger we're in for is gonna be brutal...

And now... off to catch up with the thread. Looking forward to seeing what everyone thinks about this one.

spoilers.title: Post-0.51 Thoughts
spoilers.html:
General Thoughts: I really enjoyed this one! It wasn't nearly as depressing as the last update was. For the most part, it was definitely set-up for the upcoming Beach Reset, but we did get some interesting moments here, especially with Nao-chan. More on that later.

I'm glad that the two of them can finally have a real discussion and get some semblance of closure on their issues... even if they still have a long way to go. Oh, and Yumi finally got that 10K! Didn't really expect that to ever get referenced again, but hey! Good for her.

I'm sooo glad that Makoto is taking a more active role and is pitching ideas for what they can do about the time loops, even if she clearly doesn't want to actually do anything about them. I'm also glad she brought up the possibility that the rooftop may not even be necessary to carry memories over, because if and when a Reset does occur at the Beach, they may not have a choice about fleeing to the Rooftop or not.

What'll they do? Take a bus, limo or some other vehicle back to the school while Sensei and everyone else are either gone or tripping balls? Doubtful.

I'm very intrigued to see how that's gonna play out...

Also, don't you lie, Rin. You were totally jealous. (Side note: I'm so glad her hair is back to normal.)

Uh huh... Uh huh... Futaba's back to writing stories to boost her self-esteem, we get verbal confirmation once again that her parents are still missing... all seems as expected here-

What the fuck!?



You mean to tell me there are cameras watching Kumon-mi's every move? HimawariCo ones at that?? That- That... kind of explains a lot, actually. How the simulation is being monitored (assuming you even subscribe to that theory) or perhaps the entire game is a TV show for someone or something's entertainment.

It's kind of like Makoto's analogy about the ant farm... or how Nao (not Nao-chan) basically alluded to the same exact thing during "Mother's Milk"... Not to mention the Untitled Children's Show is a thing that exists too...

Yeahhhh... I think 'cosmic TV show' is the theory I'm leaning towards right now as far as what the hell is going on in general. Perhaps the simulation theory can still work if you combine elements from both, though.

Regardless, we know that Kumon-mi is being monitored. That's for certain. This isn't the last time we hear about HimawariCo in the update either.

Her event was alright. I'm sure the Miku fans out there are happy she can get another shot at lewd content that isn't orchestrated by Nodoka, but tbh, this was more for the fan service. I like the sex scenes in this game, but really, it's secondary to everything else that's going on.

That conversation was way less chaotic than I expected... With Akira and Ami both, really. But mostly Ami. Kind of interesting that Ami would feel more comfortable with Wakana in the mother role at her house than Niki, but I suppose it makes some amount of sense. Unless Ami was just out to fluster and confuse Wakana to escape the conversation... That would be a total Arakawa thing to do.

I really don't know what to say about Ami this time. We didn't get a whole lot, but... maybe she'll try and talk with Akira during the Beach Trip? I don't see why she wouldn't. A Reset is the perfect time to see more of Ami and her motivations. Guess we'll see.

Talk about cuckoo for Cocoa Puffs, amirite?

Lol nah but seriously, what a sad fucking situation... She's still stuck on this idea that Sensei loves her the most. And I suppose in his own warped way, he does love her like he loves so many other girls. But it's just... not sustainable, and it's a downright tragedy to see how much she's changed since Chapter 1. What friends does she even have now? I mean, I suppose Rin at this point and that's it.

Yumi has been distant ever since Chika got rabies and has buddied up more to Noriko by now, and... I dunno, can you call her Maid Cafe co-workers friends of hers? They're friendly, sure (except for Ami), but they aren't like... actual close friends. Which tbh, she needs more than ever. It doesn't just affect her, but it affects Chinami too, which we can evidently see throughout both of their events.

I truly hope she improves at some point, man, but I don't see it happening anytime soon unless Reset shenanigans happen or something.

...On a brighter note, Chika's two h-scenes were pretty hot tho. As per usual. I also see Chika has done her hair up in a ponytail like she did in Chapter 1. Made me a little nostalgic. I like it. I like Yuki's new hairstyle too. And Osako's. And Noriko's.

Wow... so many good new hairstyle choices lately.

...Yeah, not gonna lie, this one was emotional. Any event involving Tsukasa is lately. I really do have a soft spot for her character and also the other Wizards.

Seriously though, just look at this response from Chinami after she finds out about Tsukasa's arranged marriage:



Their friendship is so pure, man...

Well, if you ignore the fact they were watching porn together just seconds earlier. But still, you get the idea.

Speaking more on Chinami, it seems she's the next (and last) Wizard in line to watch Akira fuck another girl in front of them. The Wizards' curiosity is now set in motion. All we can do now is... see where it all will lead.



Ugh, goddamn... That longing and vulnerable look in her eyes. Can we protect Tsukasa at all costs please? Thank you.

...Huh. It didn't really click for me until I saw these lines, but... it makes a lot of sense to see why Akira took Wizard Maya under his wing the same way Sekai did. It was his own way of paying things forward. I didn't think about such a thing at first, but yeah, that tracks...

Looks like I was wrong about Tsukasa getting a lewd scene this update, but hey... many things were at the very least set up. It's only a matter of time.



Yuki looks very cute tho...



The only unfortunate part about this is we didn't get to see it ourselves... Now if only the same could be done to Yumi's father, we'd be good.


(When talking about swimming nude in the lake ^)


This is... definitely not something I saw coming at all. Like, if you'd predicted something like Tsubasa crushing on Yuki even a few updates ago, I'd be like 'no way'. But here we are...

It's Selebus after all, and he just looooves his yuri and/or bisexual female characters. But... I dunno, man. I don't really mind this. It makes sense if you remember this is Tsubasa being herself around Yuki, someone she was able to be wild and free with years ago. Only, she had to give that freedom up in exchange for obligation...

I think it's even kinda cute to see Tsubasa this way. All we know her as is this... cold and calculating person, but really, it's evident that she was forced into this divine bullshit the same as the other major players. She's clearly trying to disrupt the world somehow, kind of like Nodoka was trying to do. Only, Tsubasa knows way more than Nodoka could ever hope to thanks to her experience.

Oh yeah... Can we also address that line from Tsubasa where she mentions wishing her and Yuki's "third" was there? Who does she mean? Akira? Sekai maybe? It would certainly explain why she apparently vowed to ‘protect Akira’. So many questions…

In any case, Tsubasa is easily one of the most interesting characters to watch these days by far.

I also wish we got to see Yuki's conversation with Sara, but it happened off-screen unfortunately, so oh well.



Pft... 'Douchefriend'. Yeah, that sums Akira up, alright.

...Huh. It seems The Old One is back for another appearance. What even is the significance of this thing? It's still very creepy looking, whatever it is... and it sure loves following Akira around.

I didn't expect that callback to the Waiting Room Reset Puzzle, but- oh look. Another reference to HimawariCo. What the heck is their deal, even...

Oh yeah, and it also turns out Nao-chan's abilities only get better:


*Snaps fingers*


She can instantly snap Akira out of blackouts (literally).

I know it may seem foolish to trust her and her existence completely, but I meannnn... I dunno. She seems like she'd be a really helpful ally for figuring these time loops out.

My only concern, though... is that it was Wires who had the map sent to Kaori's house originally which led to Nao-chan's discovery. Not only that, but he was responsible for the second map too, which led to that weird ass door in the middle of the woods on the Camping Trip.

What is Wires' end goal here? Is Nao-chan an agent of his, or is she truly just a rogue free agent? There are still many missing pieces to this puzzle...

Kaori continues to be Kaori! Only this time... she actually talks to Yumi at length! (Seriously, how did it take so long for this to happen?) Sekai continues to live in Kaori's (and Akira's) head rent free. No surprise there... It's really sad to see Kaori lose control of herself, especially now that we know what the gods are doing to her.



Sounds familiar, huh... A lot like the last year of Sekai's life, where her mind wasn't her own anymore and she felt unsafe unless Akira was around to help her calm down.

You can really see the desperation in Kaori's eyes too. She doesn't want Akira to get fed up with her and abandon her. After all, she doesn't have many friends to go around.

...Man, she needs a hug too.

Also, wow. Can I just say that there have been so many moments this update where Akira's morals in regards to the Wizards were tested?

"Hey, Papa. Chinami wants to talk about sexual stuff."
"Akira, you need to continue your lessons with Tsukasa and talk with her about sex."
"Wow, Friend! What great mating! Okay, now it's Nao-chan's turn!"

Knowing Sensei, he can only hold that back for so long... This timebomb will be an explosive one once it goes off.



Oh dayum... Kaori's kinkiness knows no bounds.




Okay, so this one is interesting... because like, once Akira picks Nao up from Wakana and Osako's place, they talk alone in Kaori's apartment. And after a surprisingly insightful conversation, Akira says, "it'll take a miracle to figure out this world" or something along those lines. And Nao-chan's response?

"I will be your miracle."

Which brings us to this event, and... wow. I'm glad I decided to save this event for last, because... this one left me with lots to think about. (BTW, major props to Moonflare for the trigger guide as always.)

So Maya starts out masturbating in her room, right? Pretty hot stuff. Then she gets a knock on her door, thinking it to be Sensei, but nope! Surprise! It's Nao-chan. Pretty weird and jarring right off the bat, but then the weird shit happens.

Everything glitches out when the dorm room door opens, then even Moyo and Maya 2 show up. Maya gets pushed into the strange abyss and...

Suddenly we're right back at the first event of the entire game: "Every Day I Grow Some More". Only it's not Sensei this time, it's Maya in his place. And Nao-chan is Ami and Akira is Maya, and... yeah, it's pretty crazy. It almost feels like a Maya TSS event, even though it technically isn't one by name.

The entire goal of this is for Nao to get Maya on the correct path again so that maybe she can regain her memories as Maya Prime, or perhaps even become an even better Maya by the end of it all. Maya doesn't seem to get it, but at the very least, this should get Maya thinking. And perfect timing too! Right before the Beach two-parter.

When Nao said to Akira that she would be 'his miracle', I interpreted this as her saying that she'd help him get Maya Prime back in some capacity so that he can find hope and courage of some kind again. Who knows how effective this will have turned out... Maybe next month we'll get some sort of idea.



Yes. Yes he does.

Okay, so I can't show Maya's because F95's image limit got lowered for whatever reason, but all I'll say about it is it was very nice to look at. It's cool to see Maya finally send a text after all this time. Karin too, whose conversation I found way more interesting.

And speaking of that...



Oh look! It's that same damn cat again. We truly can't escape him, can we?

Anyway, this message only has one real conversation to it, and it seems to be Karin trying to make conversation with Akira again. She essentially confirms that she'll be at the Beach with everyone else and asks him to approach her on his own, which can only mean we'll see this arc continue very soon. I very much look forward to it, because I for one love Karin and where her story's headed.

Closing thoughts: Once again, I felt that this was a solid update. There was a lot of set-up for the Beach for sure, but there were still some very interesting things revealed. Nao-chan was undoubtedly the MVP of this entire update, leaving us with many lingering questions before the long anticipated 8th Reset...

We're in for another wild ride... I just know it. It's almost evil that Sel is taking his vacation right in between those two parts. The inevitable cliffhanger we're in for is gonna be brutal...

This is... definitely not something I saw coming at all. Like, if you'd predicted something like Tsubasa crushing on Yuki even a few updates ago, I'd be like 'no way'. But here we are...

It's Selebus after all, and he just looooves his yuri and/or bisexual female characters. But... I dunno, man. I don't really mind this. It makes sense if you remember this is Tsubasa being herself around Yuki, someone she was able to be wild and free with years ago. Only, she had to give that freedom up in exchange for obligation...

I think it's even kinda cute to see Tsubasa this way. All we know her as is this... cold and calculating person, but really, it's evident that she was forced into this divine bullshit the same as the other major players. Oh yeah... Can we also address that line from Tsubasa where she mentions wishing her and Yuki's "third" was there? Who does she mean? Akira? Sekai maybe? It would certainly explain why she apparently vowed to ‘protect Akira’. So many questions…

In any case, Tsubasa is easily one of the most interesting characters to watch these days by far.

I also wish we got to see Yuki's conversation with Sara, but it happened off-screen unfortunately, so oh well.

spoilers.title: Osako is actually hilarious
Nao-chan Part 2: That event with Maya
spoilers.html:
Okay, so this one is interesting... because like, once Akira picks Nao up from Wakana and Osako's place, they talk alone in Kaori's apartment. And after a surprisingly insightful conversation, Akira says, "it'll take a miracle to figure out this world" or something along those lines. And Nao-chan's response?

"I will be your miracle."

Which brings us to this event, and... wow. I'm glad I decided to save this event for last, because... this one left me with lots to think about. (BTW, major props to Moonflare for the trigger guide as always.)

So Maya starts out masturbating in her room, right? Pretty hot stuff. Then she gets a knock on her door, thinking it to be Sensei, but nope! Surprise! It's Nao-chan. Pretty weird and jarring right off the bat, but then the weird shit happens.

Everything glitches out when the dorm room door opens, then even Moyo and Maya 2 show up. Maya gets pushed into the strange abyss and...

Suddenly we're right back at the first event of the entire game: "Every Day I Grow Some More". Only it's not Sensei this time, it's Maya in his place. And Nao-chan is Ami and Akira is Maya, and... yeah, it's pretty crazy. It almost feels like a Maya TSS event, even though it technically isn't one by name.

The entire goal of this is for Nao to get Maya on the correct path again so that maybe she can regain her memories as Maya Prime, or perhaps even become an even better Maya by the end of it all. Maya doesn't seem to get it, but at the very least, this should get Maya thinking. And perfect timing too! Right before the Beach two-parter.

When Nao said to Akira that she would be 'his miracle', I interpreted this as her saying that she'd help him get Maya Prime back in some capacity so that he can find hope and courage of some kind again. Who knows how effective this will have turned out... Maybe next month we'll get some sort of idea.

posts.content_text_full: Probably a low IQ question, but I have only ever downloaded the whole game each time for a patch I just need to download the patch then merge the game folder? Also are the "Care packages" the DLC? Do I just do the same?

posts.content_html_raw:
To install an update, simply download the "update", then replace the files on the game directory.

Care Packages (which are dlc) are divided in two categories: old care packages, and 2025 "fanfest" care packages. The 2025 one you can just put inside the game directory, they are worth it. The old ones come with DRM, which will destroy your saves - needing you to install the anti-drm patch.

*do mind that it has become a general agreement that the old care packages are just not worth the hassle, and even if you do want to see them, we recommend that you do so in a separate (cloned) game directory and either keep them there, or just delete them after.

**also do mind that some of the content for the care packages are not viewable in-game, but are rather pdfs and jpgs inside the folder structure.

Question how exactly do i add that save file from a few pages ago to my downloaded game data?
Click to expand...
Renpy saves in two separate locations. First one is the easiest. Either go to:
1. locate your game directory (wherever you installed it), the structure should be "lessons in love (or whatever you named it)">"game">"saves". Just drop the file there.

2. Locate your system drive, the structure should be "C: (it's usually C)" > "Users" > "your user name" > "AppData" > "Roaming" > "Renpy" > "Test 2 (this is the name Selebus gave LessonsInLove in the registry)". Drop the file there.

Now, the name of the file dictates in what page it will be. If it's "1-1-LT1", it will be the first page, in the first spot. If it's "9-6-LT1", it will be the 9th page, in the 6th spot.
Edit: I have updated the guide with these instructions.

Not necessarily, but it seems that way. Sekai likely would have been 10 years older than Akira, which would put her at around Yuki/Tsubasa's age.

But at the very least it would explain Tsubasa knowing about gods, since it's been confirmed that Sekai was being assaulted by them during her last year of life.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just finished the update yesterday, and so here's my little appreciation/analysis of what I saw. Also, as a reminder, don't open these spoilers if you haven't done the last update (0.51).

What can I say? I love her! And I'm very pleased with what she brought. But at the same time, it makes me despise Sensei as a character, with all the information he withheld. I mean, her whole plan to get caught by her mother to test the limits of the sandbox might be good... if Nodoka hadn't already tested it—and failed doing so.
This world seems to love sexual intercourse, especially the deprived kind, so doing that is exactly what the «world» wants.

Also, I'm surprised she didn't notice that everyone acknowledges and «accepts» the harem. And actively hitting on Sensei, even in public. That interaction with Rin shows it clearly! What happened to the «secrecy» of the relationship?


Overall, even if someone finally wants to try something, I'm still left hungry. Since she knows you can't talk about the reset with others, why didn't she try to... write about the reset and have someone read it?


I hope that will happen... I truly hope so.
She's still a mystery, but she doesn't seem hostile or a latent danger. My thoughts about her being «sent» by something or someone are reinforced by what she does.


It may come from Sekai, but it seems to be true. The way she handles things, her reactions, the way she «snaps» Sensei when he «zones out», etc., all point to that.
There's more to say about her, of course, but I think these two screenshots sum it up well:


I'm still weirded out by how things are evolving with her. It feels «wrong», forced...
BUT, we can now choose a name with her! For my own amusement, I didn't pick an historical German name, or title, but one that fits Sensei quite well: Shub-Niggurath. Yes, I love Howard Phillips Lovecraft.
Unfortunately, during that scene, it doesn't seem like she calls him that, so I'm kinda sad.
Also, Sensei being an ass :

She'll be the main focus of my «Mix of thoughts». But for now, I'll just say one thing :


Where does it come from? Seriously? «KIND»? Him?
Intelligent, creative... I don't agree, but okay... but kind? He's not «kind», he's broken. Lost even. But certainly not «kind».
Here we are, the emotional turmoil.
Tsukasa and Chinami are both very cute, really. And as children, they're well-written (though my knowledge of children is limited to how they're made, so you might disagree). But their «lust awakening»... I don't really understand it, especially for Chinami.
I mean, Tsukasa searching for porn videos on the internet (something I did at 7 years old in school, so I won't judge) with Chinami... and that didn't activate the «lust»? They're real people in those videos, even if they're actors.
The heat you feel when you see people you know having sexual intercourse isn't just «lust»; it's also—and mostly—the excitement from the «forbidden». At least, that's my understanding.
So, I don't understand why seeing a video with Tsukasa didn't activate it, but seeing her «adoptive» father and her sister directly made her curious...
It's... too abrupt. Artificial, even.



That also seems artificial. And Chika's reaction when she realizes Chinami «saw» is just... off? I don't know, but considering that Chinami watches Game of Thrones (and certainly other shows), it's weird that this happens NOW. Chinami already knows about sex; she wasn't interested until now, but she knew about it. She's not dumb!
But...


That's why, for me, it was an emotional turmoil. Just for that. I love that scene, that picture.
After all that, I'm kinda upset with the writing in this update. Not because it's badly written (it's quite the opposite), but how the characters just fall into their archetypes. And that line of thought comes through with Touka and those sentences :



That really set me off. It feels forced, considering her previous development. She was responsible, protective—maybe motherly with Yasu, but not with Sensei.
But now, she is? The last time she interacted with him was in the dungeon (if I remember correctly), and she didn't sound motherly then (but I'm Belgian; maybe it's different in America). So... yeah, it feels off.
And it's weird because, for other characters, the continuity is solid. With Osako, for example, all her dialogue feels «natural» and was well-written.



That made me smile!
But at the same time, during the dialogue between Wakana and Ami :


It feels like it's trying to say : «You see? She might join the harem!»... And the fact that she «plays» with Ami about naming Sensei «husband» during that discussion... is this still Wakana?
So yeah, the further we go, the thinner the continuity gets. Every scene is still well-written on its own, but only some characters manage to stay consistent.

That's all from me. I've written a lot... and all in English (I'll applaud myself later) without using a dictionary or Google Translate. A small achievement!
(I lied a little, I've ask an AI to re-read my text, but I've read the result and do the correction manually. So, it's still all from me.)

There are 35 girls and he will "romance" all of them, though many girls have not been yet and there are a few you can choose not to romance. There will eventually be "purity routes" for each girl which will be like a retelling of the story wherein the MC is exclusively with that character but we're years away from them being developed and introduced.

As things are the nature of the relationships vary a lot from girl-to-girl - some are more "romantic" than others whilst some are more sexually oriented. Some start off romantically but inevitably get less so; most likely all the relationships in the game will go downhill at some point or another.

This is a very long game (your first playthrough will probably take 150 or so hours) and it's not really a porn game (well, technically it's a porn game but it's not a game to go to if wanking is your goal). There's a lot of disturbing content and the game explores heavy themes like sexual abuse, grooming, that kind of thing. The MC is a sexual predator and the game does not obfuscate that fact. It's an amazing game but if your interest is porn and/or feelgood romance then yeah, it's probably not what you're looking for lol

Now, I'm not about to dissect similarities because, again, I didn't like the game and barely remember it. I'd have to replay it in order to do that, and it simply didn't appeal to me. I will say though that the reason I didn't like the game had nothing to do with it being similar to LiL or anything like that, but because I had glaring issues with the plot.

I will offer an example from what I do remember. Specifically, there is this one event where dude goes:
"Man, I still feel like a piece of shit because I was dating this girl, and so I distanced a bit from my friends. One day we went away for the weekend and I left my phone at home. When I got back, there was this text message from 2 days before from one of my friends saying she needed me cause her father died. So I rushed to her home as soon as I read it. But, man, I'll never forgive myself! I should have been there for her earlier! I should have known better than to leave my phone at home! I'm such a horrible person!"

View attachment 3785462 View attachment 3785465

View attachment 3785471 View attachment 3785475 And here I am reading this and thinking to myself "what is wrong with you?" lol Didn't you rush there as soon as you knew about it? That's basically what a good friend does, how are you guilty of not having anticipated that her father would die and that you needed to take your phone with you? I mean sure, maybe you could have wanted to know sooner, but if the author wanted him to feel guilty why not do it right?

Cause this is my biggest issue as far as I can remember: the writing. It's just that this event is so obvious: the correct/much stronger writing choice here would be: Dude sees the fucking message as soon as it arrives, because he takes the phone with him (why the hell would he leave a cellphone at home in the first place? super convoluted plot reason), but dismisses it as nothing serious because of his girlfriend time, and then when he learns what that was about he rushes there in guilt. Now he's guilty of something.

Hey, you want him to be a real jackass? Make him realise that it was serious, but whatever it was he'd deal with it after the trip. Maybe he finds out that something serious happened on the same night he's about to have sex with his girlfriend for the first time, and he chooses to ignore his phone. Then, if you really want to fuck with the plot, you make the childhood friend kiss him out of desperation and grief, and he lets her because he feels guilty about not being there for her, at the same time he's thinking about how he's betraying his girlfriend that just gave him her virginity. Anyway, the writing is weak.

And if you read the ramble, that's the problem with taking inspiration from a piece of work that is much more than assets, themes, and imagery. Cause in terms of game design, this one is probably better than LiL. But LiL is what it is because it excels in writing, and if you take inspiration from something then it's gonna be compared to that. And yeah, the writing isn't good here (although it's clearly trying to be). That's the issue for me, because this isn't a story about Akira, it's its own thing more or less and if the story was compelling I'd be super happy about it. But it's not good enough to be taken seriously, and it isn't silly enough to be taken lightly - at times, being perfectly honest, it reads like fanfiction.

Now, this is my take - if someone enjoyed the game, more power to them - I spent time in it, and I sure wish I had. Hell, I wish we had 30 more Lost in Yous, cause if we did, chances are I'd enjoy some of them myself. So I hope the author finds success in his game, and that his writing skill continues improving.

posts.content_html_raw:
Ok, so I'm a bit late, I haven't had time to read .50 until now, and I just finished it.
First, I have a question. I'm on the red path. None of Sara's 3 events will clear this update; I know they're supposed to get crossed out, but they won't even do that. I'm just stuck with 3 Sara events that won't go away. Any ideas?

Next, I have some thoughts.

I'm glad Noriko finally got some action and was floored when Niki walked in. This blow-up was probably one of my most anticipated moments for both characters for me, only for it to end up being nothing more than a hallway pity party. While I'm sure this will have long-lasting effects for the sisters, it already feels like we're on our way to sweeping it under the rug, so it's kind of a letdown in that regard. On top of that, the "I'm a monster" and "lock me up" conversations have happened so often that they've lost all impact. I'm starting to believe that Sel is running out of ideas on how to have the adults react to finding out. What really stood out to me was Ami's involvement in this, the little red monster really stepped on some toes this time, and I'm glad that it sort of backfired on her. I'd definitely call her the highlight of the update.

Specifically the Yuki gangbang scene. So usually I'm all down for non-con gangbangs in my H games. Hell, Lona RPG is one of my favorites, so take it from me, this one kind of sucked. Visually, there's only so much you can do with faceless, nondescript blobs, so it looked more strange than shocking, and narratively, it doesn't really add anything to Yuki. I doubt that the game will spare any amount of time developing Mr. Yakuza Boss, and he will probably get written out of the game sooner or later. It just kind of feels lazy, imo.

The way this guy talks, you would almost believe that he is in fact writing Akira going down that path, but in reality it's been over 3 million words of "will he, won't he" meandering as he gives him constant justifications and many factors enabling him to do it, in extremely contrived ways too (like the whole Tsubasa arc currently going), while he himself displays inconsistent attitude towards it. Sel can never commit to whether he wants Akira to have a progression or regression arc and quite frankly it's gotten boring a long time ago, especially with how incoherent the transition between those mentalities is. Akira could be sinking in depravity one event, and in the next one he'd be acting like that never happened. It'd be one thing if this was Chapter 1 or even 2, but again, failure to commit to a direction of your protagonist and narrative in general after 3 million words is not impressive, to say the least.

It also seems to me like he's ignoring a lot of earlier implications that Akira felt such deep guilt for what he did to "the girl he's so obsessed with" that it would actually make sense for him not to go down that route again. But alas, this is coming from the writer who plays favorites and thinks the characters who have suffered the most are shitty people while the most privileged ones are the epitome of "kindness and empathy".
